title: ECS Health & Safety
subtitle: Fifteen copied ElectricianTraining ECS mock and topic tests
description: A source-matched ECS health and safety exam set copied from the ElectricianTraining mock and topic tests. It covers the full ECS safety spread: electrotechnical safety, special site hazards, work equipment, working at height, fire, hygiene, PPE, accident reporting, manual handling, general health and safety and environmental practice.
format: Fifteen rotating source tests: four full ECS mocks plus eleven topic tests. The category pass threshold is set at 86%, matching the full ECS mock standard.

sections.title: ElectricianTraining ECS Health & Safety Mock Exams

questions.prompt: If you discover a hole or gap in a fire rated wall or floor that has not been fire-stopped, what should you do?

options.A: Cover the hole or gap with insulating tape
options.B: Ignore it unless it is causing a draught
options.C: Report it to your supervisor without delay
options.D: Use decorators' sealant to fill the gap

questions.explanation: Supervisors need to be made aware of any observed inadequacies in fire-stopping - which can undermine fire precautions catastrophically during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

questions.prompt: In addition to preserving fire separation between areas of a building, which other important fire safety function can fire-stopping achieve?
questions.explanation: Many structural elements, such as timber joists or steel beams, lose strength quickly when exposed to fire and rely on linings like plasterboard for protection. Fire-stopping the gaps where services pass through maintains that protection, helping prevent premature structural collapse and giving occupants time to escape safely.

questions.prompt: Intumescent materials used to provide fire-stopping are designed to:
questions.explanation: A limited number of fire-resistant materials may be used to provide fire-stopping. These include intumescent products, which are designed to expand and provide fire-stopping when subjected to heat. Examples include intumescent 'pillows' (used to provide internal sealing of trunking) and intumescent mastic.

questions.prompt: The purpose of fire-stopping in a building is to:

options.B: Delay the passage of fire and smoke through openings in walls and floors

questions.explanation: Fire-stopping is a passive fire protection measure used to seal any openings created in a fire resistance-rated wall or floor assembly, e.g. to allow pipes or wiring systems to pass through. During fire conditions this will impede the spread of fire and smoke.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you disturb fire-stopping around a wiring system penetrating a wall or floor whilst carrying out work?

options.A: Ensure that the fire-stopping is reinstated to the necessary standard as soon as possible
options.B: Fill any holes or gaps with squashed paper
options.D: Nail a piece of wood over any gaps

questions.explanation: It is essential that the integrity of fire compartments is maintained during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Compromising compartmentation, such as failing to adequately fire-stop (seal) openings for services to pass through, can undermine fire precautions catastrophically. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does NOT help sustainability during construction projects?

options.B: Leaving engines and motors running when they are not needed
options.D: Vehicle sharing or using public transport to get to work

questions.explanation: Leaving engines and motors running wastes fuel, creates avoidable emissions and adds unnecessary site noise. Switching plant off when it is not needed is the sustainable choice.

questions.prompt: From an environmental point of view, why should materials be reused, where possible?

options.A: A lot of energy and raw materials go into making most construction products
options.B: It makes less mess on site

questions.explanation: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the re-use of materials can also contribute to effective waste management.

questions.prompt: You are on site and you need to dispose of some waste liquid that has oil in it and you are not sure what to do with it. What should you do?

options.A: Ask your supervisor about the correct way to deal with this waste.
options.B: Dispose of it in a sealed container into the site skip
options.C: Pour it onto the ground, it will soak away
options.D: Take it outside and set light to it

questions.explanation: Dealing with hazardous/special waste will include proper storage and segregation before it is taken away by an authorized waste carrier as required by environmental legislation. An oil spillage could also get into the ground or drains, which may also be an offence under environmental law. Burning waste on site is also an offence, under air pollution legislation, and can lead to local complaints.

questions.prompt: A portable electric generator on site has two power outlets, 110 volts and 230 volts. What colour would the 110 volt outlet be?
questions.explanation: On UK sites a standard colour code identifies supply voltages at a glance for safety. Yellow denotes 110 V reduced low voltage equipment, so the 110 V outlet, its plugs and connectors are yellow, while 230 V kit uses blue, clearly separating the safer site supply from the higher mains voltage.

questions.prompt: What is the most serious effect that electric shock can have if you come into contact with a live part?

options.A: The electric current can cause a slight tingling in the fingers
options.B: The electric current can cause burn marks on the fingers
options.C: The electric current can cause the finger muscles to twitch
options.D: The electric current can cause the heart to stop, resulting in death

questions.explanation: Contact with live electrical parts can be fatal. If you do not know otherwise, always assume that electrical parts are live.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does the Electricity at Work (EAW) regulations apply to?

options.A: All persons engaged for work purposes

questions.explanation: The EAW Regulations impose duties on employers, employees and the self employed.

questions.prompt: In accordance with the Electricity at Work regulations, when considering whether to work live a responsible person should:
questions.explanation: To identify and assess the risks involved and the methods of controlling them.

questions.prompt: When is live working permissible?

options.A: When it is unreasonable in all circumstances for the equipment to be made dead and suitable precautions are taken
options.B: When the means of isolation cannot be identified
options.C: When the person carrying out the work is a competent person
options.D: When the person working on the equipment is wearing rubber gloves

questions.explanation: This is a requirement under r.14 of the EAW Regulations. However, it does not mean that live working is then 'safe'

questions.prompt: With regard to the effect of electrical current on the human body, one of the following is correct:

options.A: A 3 amp fuse should prevent a person receiving a fatal electric shock
options.B: A 30mA Residual Current Device (RCD) should prevent a person receiving a fatal electric shock.
options.C: A 5 amp rewireable fuse should prevent a person receiving a fatal electric shock
options.D: A 6 amp circuit breaker should prevent a person receiving a fatal electric shock

questions.explanation: An RCD is a mechanical switching device intended to cause the opening of the contacts when the residual current attains a given value under specified conditions.

questions.prompt: You have to enter a manhole in which you believe there could be toxic gases. You have not been provided with any Respiratory Protective Equipment (RPE). What should you do?

options.A: Just get on with the job, and accept the risks
options.B: Look into the manhole to see if you can see any harmful gases
options.C: Sniff the atmosphere in the manhole to see if you can smell harmful gases
options.D: Tell your supervisor that you will need RPE, and if necessary, training in confined space working

questions.explanation: An employer must provide all necessary personal protective equipment and respiratory protective equipment when an employee is required to enter a confined space. This is one of the requirements of the Confined Spaces Regulations 1997.

questions.prompt: When working alone:

options.A: Don't bother anyone if you have a problem, always sort it out yourself
options.B: Make sure someone responsible knows where you are
options.C: Wear headphones, it will make the day go more quickly
options.D: You can do away with protective equipment

questions.explanation: Employees should adhere to safe working arrangements put in place by their employer. When working alone, such arrangements should include informing a responsible person of your location periodically.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred nominal voltage for portable hand tools on construction sites?
questions.explanation: Construction sites use 110 V centre-tapped-to-earth supplies for portable tools because this limits the voltage to earth to around 55 V, greatly reducing the severity of any electric shock in the damp, hazardous site environment while still powering tools effectively.

questions.prompt: What is most commonly used to reduce 230 volts to 110 volts on site?
questions.explanation: A transformer, usually coloured yellow, will transform 230 volts (mains voltage) down to a relatively safe 110 volts.

questions.prompt: If an extension cable is to be run across a site road, what action should you take?

options.A: Don't do anything to protect the cable
options.B: Lay the cable over wooden boards
options.C: Place a rubber protection ramp over it and put up a sign stating 'Ramp Ahead'

questions.explanation: It is essential that the cable is protected from damage caused by passing traffic. A sign will warn road traffic of the ramp.

questions.prompt: Why may a confined space be dangerous to work in?

options.A: Air in the space may be unbreathable due to poisonous gas
options.C: Temperature and poor ventilation may affect the worker
options.D: There may not be sufficient working space

questions.explanation: There can be a range of hazards associated with confined spaces, and these can include all of those mentioned

questions.prompt: Prior to moving a mobile tower scaffold, the platform height should reduced to a maximum of:
questions.explanation: This figure is quoted in guidance published by the HSE and PASMA. Checks should also be made that there are no obstructions overhead, the ground is firm, level and free from potholes, it is not too windy and there are no people or materials on the tower.

questions.prompt: What do the letters SWL stand for?
questions.explanation: Machinery and accessories for lifting loads should be clearly marked to indicate their safe working loads.

questions.prompt: When working above public areas, what should be considered?

options.A: Keeping the areas open to the public

questions.explanation: There is a significant risk to the public from falling materials, if this is not considered before and during work.

questions.prompt: You have been asked to operate a cherry-picker (mobile elevated work platform) when it is very windy. What should your FIRST consideration be?

options.A: Does the wind-speed make it unsafe to use the machine
options.B: Tie all light-weight objects to the hand-rails of the basket
options.C: Wear a safety harness and clip it to the structure that you are working on
options.D: Wear an extra layer of clothing to keep warm

questions.explanation: The priority in safety is eliminating risk at source - in this case by not working in dangerous conditions - rather than trying to stay safe by using protective equipment.

questions.prompt: How many people should be working on a ladder at one time?

options.B: One on each section of an extension ladder
options.C: Three if it is long enough

questions.explanation: Only one person should be working on a ladder, although another person may be footing it, for extra stability.

questions.prompt: What is the ideal angle for a ladder against a wall and floor?

options.A: Four metres up for every metre out from the wall
options.B: One metre up for every metre out from the wall
options.C: One metre up for every two metres out from the wall
options.D: Two metres up for every metre out from the wall

questions.explanation: The correct angle for a ladder is 75 degrees, which an be judged using the angle indicator marked on the stiles of some ladders or using the 1 in 4 rule.

questions.prompt: How often should a first-aider qualified in First Aid at Work (FAW) or Emergency First Aid at Work (EFAW) receive retraining?
questions.explanation: First Aid at Work (FAW) and Emergency First Aid at Work (EFAW) certificates are valid for three years and first-aiders are required to undertake retraining at the end of this period. However, the HSE also strongly recommends that first-aiders undertake annual (half-day) refresher training.

questions.prompt: A person nearly collapses complaining of stomach pains. What should you do?

options.A: Ask them if they want something to eat
options.B: Go and find them something to drink
options.C: Help them to find somewhere comfortable to sit

questions.explanation: Unexplained collapse with severe stomach pain could signal a serious medical emergency, so the priority is to get trained help fast. Sending someone for the first-aider brings competent assessment quickly; offering food or drink could be harmful if the casualty needs treatment or surgery.

questions.prompt: Where would you go in the event of a fire?

options.A: To the canteen for a cup of tea
options.C: To the fire to see what is going on

questions.explanation: Going to the designated fire assembly point lets marshals carry out a roll call and confirm everyone is safely out, so no one is wrongly believed still inside. Staying near the fire or wandering to huts puts you at risk and disrupts the head count.

questions.prompt: What must your employer do if the daily personal noise exposure is at or exceeds 85 db(A)?

options.A: Issue hearing protection to those exposed and ensure that it is worn
options.B: Provide hearing protection to those employees who ask for it
options.C: Report it to the Health and Safety Executive
options.D: Tell employees to buy their own hearing protection

questions.explanation: This is an interim measure under the Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005 when the daily personal noise exposure is at or exceeds the upper exposure action value of 85 dB(A). Exposure should subsequently be reduced by implementing organizational or technical measures.

questions.prompt: Which of the following animals can carry Weil's disease?
questions.explanation: Weil's disease is a serious and sometimes fatal infection that can be transmitted to humans by contact with infected rats. Another form of Leptospirosis infection can be transmitted from cattle to humans.

questions.prompt: An emergency route(s) must be provided on construction sites to ensure:

options.A: Safe passage to a secure place of safety
options.B: Safe passage to the ground from height
options.C: Safe passage to the open air
options.D: Safe passage to the rest area

questions.explanation: Emergency routes exist so people can reach a secure place of safety quickly if danger arises, not merely escape from height or reach a rest area. The aim is a clear, protected path leading away from harm to somewhere genuinely safe.

questions.prompt: Exposure to asbestos fibres may cause which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Breathing in asbestos fibres can also lead to a number of other diseases, including lung cancer and mesothelioma

questions.prompt: How can you protect your eyesight while working on site?

options.A: By not looking directly at what you are doing
options.D: By wearing the correct type of eye protection

questions.explanation: Only eye protection matched to the hazard, such as impact goggles or a face shield, physically shields the eyes from flying particles, dust, arc flash or chemicals. Squinting or avoiding looking does nothing to stop debris, and sunglasses offer no impact protection.

questions.prompt: When considering what measures to take to protect people's health and safety, PPE should always be regarded as:

options.A: The best way to tackle the job

questions.explanation: Engineering controls and safe systems of work should always be considered first.

questions.prompt: When an employee has been issued with eye protection, what are their duties under the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations?

options.A: Not to loan the equipment to other operatives
options.B: To ensure that they are the right type of protector
options.C: To pay for replacement of lost eye protection
options.D: To use the protection in accordance with training and instruction

questions.explanation: Regulation 10(2) requires that every employee shall use any PPE in accordance with the training and instruction received.

questions.prompt: Who should you report serious accidents to?
questions.explanation: Your employer or supervisor must be told so they can record the incident, arrange help, and meet legal duties to report certain injuries to the HSE under RIDDOR. A workmate has no authority to act, and police or ambulance handle emergencies, not workplace reporting.

questions.prompt: In hot weather which one of the following is correct with regard to safety helmets?

options.A: You can drill holes in your safety hat for ventilation
options.B: You can take off your helmet while working inside the building
options.C: You do not need to wear your helmet
options.D: You must continue to wear your helmet

questions.explanation: On construction sites, despite controls being put in place, there will always be situations where a risk of head injury remains. Taking off your helmet would put you at a much greater risk of a head injury and any unauthorised modification would be in breach of legal requirements and could render the helmet next to useless.

questions.prompt: When a person is injured at work, who should enter the details in the accident book?

options.A: The injured person or anyone acting for them

questions.explanation: This is the procedure for recording accidents internally in the accident book(BI 510).

questions.prompt: When judging "individual capability" for manual handling, you should assume:
questions.explanation: Assessing ability for manual handling must be done on an individual basis.

questions.prompt: Why should a serious accident be reported to the enforcing authority?

options.A: It helps the site find out what caused it
options.C: So that the company will be held responsible
options.D: So that the site manager can see who is to blame

questions.explanation: Serious accidents (specified injuries or those resulting in an absence of over 7 days) must be reported to the enforcing authority under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR).

questions.prompt: What is the MAXIMUM weight that an individual may lift?

options.A: 15kg provided that it is a compact load
options.B: 35kg provided that it has no sharp edges
options.C: The weight they can lift comfortably

questions.explanation: There are no strict weight limits - the priority is to avoid injury.

questions.prompt: As an approximate guide the manual handling capacity of a two person team is:

options.A: The capacity of the strongest individual
options.B: The capacity of the weakest individual
options.C: The sum of their individual capacities
options.D: Two thirds the sum of their individual capacities

questions.explanation: This is contained in HSE guidance on the Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992.

questions.prompt: Why would your supervisor ask you to read the method statement and risk assessment before you start your next job?

options.A: As someone has taken the time and trouble to write them, you might as well read them
options.B: He thinks you have got nothing better to do
options.C: He wouldn't, he thinks they are a waste of time
options.D: They contain information on how to carry out the job in a safe manner

questions.explanation: The supervisor must, by law, keep workers advised of significant risks, and control measures.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations require the colour coding of signs. What colours are used on a sign indicating a warning, for example "Fork-lift trucks operating"?
questions.explanation: Warning signs use yellow with black, a high-contrast combination that grabs attention and signals a hazard to be cautious of. Blue means mandatory, red means prohibition or fire, and green means safe condition, so those colours carry different meanings.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations require the colour coding of safety signs. What colours are used on a sign indicating a safe condition, for example "First Aid kit"?
questions.explanation: Emergency escape and first-aid signs are rectangular or square and feature a white pictogram on a green background.

questions.prompt: If there is a risk of injury from lifting loads what should you think about first?

options.B: What the weight of the load is
options.C: Where to hold the load when lifting
options.D: Whether the load needs to be lifted at all

questions.explanation: If possible, it is best to avoid the risks from lifting altogether. This is the preferred requirement laid down in the Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992.

questions.prompt: Regulations that govern health and safety on construction sites:

options.D: Do not apply during 'out of hours' working

questions.explanation: The requirements of health and safety law are mandatory, and failure to follow them can lead to prosecutions.

questions.prompt: What happens if a Prohibition Notice is issued by an Inspector of the local authority or the HSE?

options.A: The work can continue if adequate safety precautions are put in place
options.B: The work can continue, provided a risk assessment is carried out
options.C: The work in hand can be completed, but no new work started
options.D: The work that is subject to the notice must cease

questions.explanation: The work activity covered by a prohibition notice must cease, until the identified danger is removed.

questions.prompt: If a Health and Safety Executive Inspector issues a "Prohibition Notice", this means that:

options.A: Specific work activities, highlighted on the notice, must stop
options.B: The HSE must supervise all work from then on
options.C: The HSE must supervise the work covered by the notice
options.D: The Site Manager can choose whether or not to ignore the notice

questions.explanation: Prohibition notices are intended to Stop activities which can cause serious injury.

questions.prompt: If you discover a hole or gap in a fire rated wall or floor that has not been fire-stopped, what should you do?

options.A: Cover the hole or gap with insulating tape
options.B: Ignore it unless it is causing a draught
options.C: Report it to your supervisor without delay
options.D: Use decorators' sealant to fill the gap

questions.explanation: Supervisors need to be made aware of any observed inadequacies in fire-stopping - which can undermine fire precautions catastrophically during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

questions.explanation: Fire-stopping protects the load-bearing structure by keeping fire and heat from reaching vulnerable elements like timber joists or steel beams, delaying collapse so occupants have time to escape. Noise, nuisance alarms and energy saving are unrelated to its fire-resistance purpose.

questions.prompt: Intumescent materials used to provide fire-stopping are designed to:
questions.explanation: A limited number of fire-resistant materials may be used to provide fire-stopping. These include intumescent products, which are designed to expand and provide fire-stopping when subjected to heat. Examples include intumescent 'pillows' (used to provide internal sealing of trunking) and intumescent mastic.

questions.prompt: What are fire-stops designed to do?

options.B: Delay the passage of fire and smoke through openings in walls and floors
options.D: Protect services (such as wiring systems) against fire damage

questions.explanation: Fire-stops are designed to maintain the fireproofing of a wall or floor assembly. Fire-stopping delays the spread of fire and, generally, the spread of smoke as well.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you disturb fire-stopping around a wiring system penetrating a wall or floor whilst carrying out work?

options.A: Ensure that the fire-stopping is reinstated to the necessary standard as soon as possible
options.B: Fill any holes or gaps with squashed paper
options.D: Nail a piece of wood over any gaps

questions.explanation: It is essential that the integrity of fire compartments is maintained during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Compromising compartmentation, such as failing to adequately fire-stop (seal) openings for services to pass through, can undermine fire precautions catastrophically. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

questions.prompt: Why should different types of waste be separated on site?

options.A: So the local council can charge Landfill Tax
options.B: So the main contractor can check what's being thrown away
options.C: So waste can be recovered more easily
options.D: They will take up less room in the skip

questions.explanation: This is good practice, since waste recovery can save both energy and materials, compared to creating brand new materials or items. It will also cut the amount of waste that goes to landfill. If the waste is classed as hazardous (special waste in Scotland) then the effective separation of different wastes is a legal requirement.

questions.prompt: Do individuals have any responsibility for sustainability when on site?

options.A: No, it is a matter for the Environment Agency/NIEA/SEPA
options.B: No, it is dealt with by the site manager
options.C: Only on sites where there is asbestos

questions.explanation: Your responsibility is to follow the site and company rules aimed at environmental protection and sustainability, and to help your company to comply with relevant legal requirements, such as the need to segregate waste properly (e.g. so that it can be recovered).

questions.prompt: Which of the following should be used to prove a circuit or equipment is dead after isolation?

options.A: A lamp holder with a length of flex attached
options.C: A proprietary test lamp or two-pole voltage detector

questions.explanation: Accident history has shown that using incorrectly set multimeters or makeshift devices for voltage detection has often caused accidents. The use of non-contact voltage indicators (voltage sticks) is also not advised as the sole means of proving dead.

questions.prompt: Which of the following procedures should be used when more than one person will be working on circuits supplied from a distribution board which has been switched off?

options.A: Blowing a horn before the power is switched on again
options.B: Giving each operative a volt stick
options.C: Telling everyone what time the power will be switched on again
options.D: The use of a multi-lock hasp on the isolator with a padlock for each operative

questions.explanation: A multi-lock hasp with one padlock per worker means the isolator cannot be re-energised until every person has finished and removed their own lock, guaranteeing no one is reconnected while still working live. Verbal warnings or timings can be misheard or forgotten.

questions.prompt: How should you get rid of hazardous/special waste?

options.A: In accordance with the correct site waste rules
options.B: Put it at the bottom of any site skip
options.C: Take it home, they won't want it on site
options.D: Take it to the nearest local authority waste tip

questions.explanation: The Hazardous Waste Regulations (Special Waste Regulations in Scotland) require hazardous/special waste to be properly segregated or otherwise treated, and then recovered or disposed of in an officially approved way.

questions.prompt: Electrical installations on construction sites should be periodically inspected and tested:
questions.explanation: Three monthly inspections of construction site installations are recommended in IEE Guidance Note 3.

questions.prompt: An electrical Permit to Work is primarily a statement that:

options.A: Certain instructions need to be followed
options.B: Someone else has taken responsibility for the work
options.C: The circuit or equipment has been isolated and is safe to work on
options.D: The circuit or equipment is live

questions.explanation: Permits to work describe the procedures that prevent a major hazard, such as electricity or moving machinery, from causing harm, usually by isolation to effectively ensure (in the case of electricity) 'dead' working with no chance of it going 'live'.

questions.prompt: The normal procedure for working on electrical equipment should be which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Dead working should be considered as the norm and work on or near live conductors should rarely be permitted

questions.prompt: The nominal single phase voltage in the UK is?
questions.explanation: This is the nominal voltage for public electricity supply systems within Europe.

questions.prompt: Before entering an excavation to start work, it must first be:
questions.explanation: Excavation work is hazardous. A competent person, knowledgeable about how to reduce risks, notably from collapse of the walls, must inspect the excavation first.

questions.prompt: You have to enter a manhole in which you know there are toxic gases. You have all the PPE but there does not appear to be a rescue plan in place. What should you do?

options.A: Ask your mate to stand-by at the top of the manhole with a length of rope
options.B: Do not enter the manhole until a rescue plan and rescue equipment are in place
options.C: Just get on and do the job, it will probably be alright
options.D: Plan to carry out the job in short bursts

questions.explanation: A rescue plan must be in place before anyone enters a confined space. This is one of the requirements of the Confined Spaces Regulations 1997.

questions.prompt: You have to walk across a site several times a day, but have to dodge a lot of site traffic. The first thing you should do is:

options.B: Jump on the back of a vehicle if you can, it's safer than walking
options.C: Tell your supervisor about the danger
options.D: Walk around the edges of the site to keep out of the way

questions.explanation: Pedestrian routes should have been set up to keep people and vehicles apart, so inform your employer if the system is not working. Don't hitch rides on vehicles unless safe seating is provided.

questions.prompt: What action should you take if an electric drill cuts out while you are using it?

options.A: Put it back into the tool box
options.B: Remove it from use and tell your supervisor
options.D: Switch the power off and on

questions.explanation: An electric drill that cuts out may have an internal fault, damaged flex, overheating problem or failing switch. Taking it out of service and reporting it prevents someone else from using unsafe equipment before it is checked.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred nominal voltage for local lighting up to 2 kW on construction sites?
questions.explanation: Reduced low voltage at 110V centre-tapped to earth limits any shock to about 55V to earth, greatly reducing danger in the harsh, often wet conditions on site. 230V and 400V carry far higher shock risk for portable equipment.

questions.prompt: To operate a powered hand tool you must be:
questions.explanation: There are no general age restrictions in legislation relating to the use of work equipment. Any person using work equipment, however, must be competent to do so, which will require initial and refresher training.

questions.prompt: Of the following, which is the poorest method of securing a ladder?

options.B: Securing the base of the ladder

questions.explanation: Footing a ladder is the last resort and should be avoided. Other more suitable access equipment should be used where practicable.

questions.prompt: Any damaged equipment must be:

options.B: Locked up so no one can use it

questions.explanation: Reporting damaged equipment to your supervisor ensures it is properly inspected, repaired or replaced and a competent person decides its fate. Simply throwing it away loses evidence of a fault, and labelling or locking it alone does not get the problem fixed.

questions.prompt: When can you work from a ladder?

options.A: For short periods and then only if it is safe to do so
options.D: When not being used for access

questions.explanation: Ladders are primarily means of access, not workplaces. They can be worked from, but only if the use of other, more suitable, work equipment is not appropriate and the task is of low risk and of short duration.

questions.prompt: On a mobile elevating work platform, what should you attach your safety harness to?

options.B: A secure anchorage point inside the platform
options.C: A strong part of the structure you are working on

questions.explanation: The priority is to stay within the platform (which is the safest place), and in any event you cannot be sure of the strength of other fixtures.

questions.prompt: What should you do if your work activity requires you to wear a full body safety harness and one is not available?

options.A: Borrow a harness from a colleague
options.B: Carry on working and hope that everything will be alright
options.C: Make a harness from items found on site
options.D: Stop work immediately and tell your supervisor that you do not have the correct PPE

questions.explanation: Always advise the supervisor if you do not have the correct PPE.

questions.prompt: In an emergency situation at work you should do what?

options.A: Ensure your work mates are all accounted for

questions.explanation: A site emergency plan should have been drawn up and you should be familiar with the emergency procedure.

questions.prompt: The type of accident that kills most construction site workers is:
questions.explanation: Although the other dangers can kill or cause injury, falling from height is the biggest cause of fatalities.

questions.prompt: If you came across an injury on site, what is the first thing you should do?

options.C: Tell the casualty to visit their doctor
options.D: Try and find out what happened

questions.explanation: Contacting a first aider gets trained, competent help to the casualty quickly, which is the priority for preserving life and preventing the injury worsening. Investigating what happened or sending them off elsewhere delays the care they need now.

questions.prompt: Your workmate suddenly gets a foreign body in the eye. What should you do?

options.B: Take your workmate to the supervisor
options.C: Use a clean handkerchief to try and remove it
options.D: Wash your hands before touching your mate's face

questions.explanation: A foreign body in the eye needs trained first-aid care; sending for the first-aider gets competent help without delay. Trying to remove it yourself with a handkerchief risks scratching the eye or driving the object in deeper, causing lasting damage.

questions.prompt: If there had been a small fire, who should you report it to?
questions.explanation: The supervisor should be aware, so that further preventative measures can be considered.

questions.prompt: What should you do if the toilets on your site are continually dirty?

options.A: Ask in a nearby cafe or pub if you can use their toilets
options.B: Find some cleaning materials and clean it up yourself
options.C: Ignore the problem - its normal on a construction site
options.D: Make sure you tell someone who can sort it out

questions.explanation: How often welfare facilities on site require cleaning will depend on the number of people on site and how quickly they get dirty. The person in control of the site should make sure someone is responsible for keeping the facilities clean and tidy.

questions.prompt: Exposure to asbestos fibres may cause which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Breathing in asbestos fibres can also lead to a number of other diseases, including lung cancer and mesothelioma

questions.prompt: The number of toilets provided on site depends on:

options.A: The duration of the work on site
options.B: The number of personnel on site
options.C: The ratio of male and female workers on site
options.D: The type of work being completed

questions.explanation: Guidance on the provision of welfare facilities is given in HSE publication 'Health and Safety in Construction'.

questions.prompt: When using personal protective equipment (PPE) legally you must do which of the following?

options.A: Clean it properly once a week
options.B: Not interfere with it or misuse it
options.C: Replace it at your own expense if it is damaged
options.D: Return it to the manufacturer when damaged

questions.explanation: Interfering with or misusing items provided in the interests of health, safety or welfare is an offence under the HSW Act 1974 (section 8)

questions.prompt: When is head protection required to be worn on a construction site to comply with the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations?

options.A: At all times except by those who are self employed
options.B: At all times unless there is no foreseeable risk of injury to the head other than by falling.
options.C: At all times unless you are working on scaffold
options.D: Only when you feel like it

questions.explanation: If there is no risk of injury to the head, then hard hats are not required by law. However, on construction sites, despite controls being in place, there will almost always be situations where a risk of head injury remains and require head protection to be worn. Site rules will also require the wearing of head protection other than in any designated safe areas.

questions.prompt: If personal protective equipment (PPE) is defective, what should you do?

options.A: Complain to the Health and Safety Inspector
options.B: Get your work mate to mend it if possible
options.C: Repair if possible and continue to use it

questions.explanation: Employees are required to report any defective PPE to their employer (PPE at Work Regulations 1992, Regulation 7)

questions.prompt: What type of eye protection would you wear when using a cartridge-operated tool, such as a nail gun?
questions.explanation: When using a cartridge-operated tool, such as a nail gun, shatter proof goggles should be worn.

questions.prompt: What is the aim of carrying out an accident investigation?

options.A: To determine the cause(s) and prevent similar accidents
options.B: To establish the cost of any damage incurred
options.C: To establish what injuries were sustained
options.D: To find out who is at fault

questions.explanation: An accident investigation should not only assess the cause, but also how similar accidents can be prevented in the future.

questions.prompt: If a person at work suffers an injury (other than a specified injury) due to an accident at work, it is reportable under RIDDOR if they are incapacitated for work for:
questions.explanation: An over-seven-day injury is one which is not a specified injury but results in the injured person being away from work or unable to do the full range of their normal duties for more than seven days (including any days they wouldn't normally be expected to work such as weekends, rest days or holidays) not counting the day of the injury itself.

questions.prompt: Before picking up a load, you should:

options.A: Ask a work mate to help you

questions.explanation: You or your employer must assess the risk of injury before lifting.

questions.prompt: If a load has an uneven centre of gravity, how should you lift it?

options.A: Keep the heaviest side of the load away from you
options.B: Keep the heaviest side of the load on the strongest arm
options.C: Keep the heaviest side of the load on the weakest arm
options.D: Keep the heaviest side of the load towards you

questions.explanation: There is less risk of injury if a weight's centre of gravity is near the torso.

questions.prompt: What should you ensure if you suffer an injury through a manual handling operation?

options.B: You get help and carry on working
options.C: You get paid for the job

questions.explanation: All injuries must be recorded in the Company accident book (BI 510)

questions.prompt: Where there has been a major change in a manual handling operation, what should the employer do?

options.C: Review the number of people involved

questions.explanation: This is a specific requirement of the Manual Handling Operations regulations 1992.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations require the colour coding of safety signs. What colours are used on a sign indicating a mandatory activity, for example "Safety helmets must be worn"?
questions.explanation: Mandatory signs use blue with white, telling you an action must be taken, such as wearing a helmet. Yellow and black means warning, red means prohibition, and green means safe condition, so each colour conveys a distinct instruction.

questions.prompt: Before performing manual lifting what is the first thing you should do?

options.C: Kick it to see if it is stable

questions.explanation: If you assess the whole task first, you will have a clear idea of possible hazards and how to overcome them, before lifting

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 and any regulations made under the Act are:

options.C: Not compulsory, but should be complied with if convenient
options.D: Practical advice for the employer to follow

questions.explanation: The requirements of health and safety law are mandatory and failure to follow them can lead to prosecution.

questions.prompt: Where should you look for Official advice on health and safety matters?

options.A: A professionally approved guide book on regulations
options.B: A set of health and safety guidelines provided by suppliers
options.C: Guidance issued by the Health and Safety Executive
options.D: The health and safety rules as laid down by the employer

questions.explanation: The HSE is the UK enforcing body and its guidance can be regarded as 'official'

questions.prompt: In the context of a risk assessment, what do you understand by the term risk?

options.B: Any work activity that can be described as dangerous
options.C: Something with the potential to cause injury
options.D: The likelihood that harm from a particular hazard will occur

questions.explanation: Hazard and risk are not the same. Risk reflects the chance of being harmed by a hazard

questions.prompt: Which one of the following must be in a company's written Health and Safety Policy:

options.A: Aims and objectives of the company
options.C: Name of the Health and Safety Adviser
options.D: Organization and arrangements in force for carrying out the health and safety policy

questions.explanation: This is a specific requirement of the Health and Safety at Work Act.

questions.prompt: What do the letters CDM stand for?

options.D: Control of Demolition and Management Regulations

questions.explanation: The CDM Regulations impose duties to manage construction projects, ensure physical safeguards are provided to prevent danger during such projects and that adequate welfare facilities are provided.

questions.prompt: In addition to preserving fire separation between areas of a building, which other important fire safety function can fire-stopping achieve?
questions.explanation: Many structural elements such as timber joists, studs and steel beams lose strength quickly in a fire and rely on their linings for protection. Fire-stopping the gaps where services pass through maintains that protection, so the structure stays standing long enough for people to escape.

questions.prompt: The purpose of fire-stopping in a building is to:

options.B: Delay the passage of fire and smoke through openings in walls and floors

questions.explanation: Fire-stopping is a passive fire protection measure used to seal any openings created in a fire resistance-rated wall or floor assembly, e.g. to allow pipes or wiring systems to pass through. During fire conditions this will impede the spread of fire and smoke.

questions.prompt: What can help to prevent harm to the environment from oil spillages?

options.A: A supply of water to flush the spill away
options.C: Store oils in an area that can catch any spills, such as a bund or a drip tray.
options.D: Turning liquid containers upside down so the top can't come off

questions.explanation: The use of a bund (fully walled storage area) or a drip tray will help any spillage to be contained in a small area for clear up. Any spillage could get into the ground or drains, which is likely to be an offence under environmental legislation.

questions.prompt: Under environmental law, which statement is true?

options.A: Companies and individuals can be prosecuted if they do not follow the law
options.B: Companies can be prosecuted, but not individuals
options.C: It is legal to disturb protected species' habitats
options.D: It is legal to transport business waste without proper paperwork

questions.explanation: Most environmental law is enforced against companies, but the regulator in the relevant part of the UK (the Environment Agency, SEPA or NIEA) can also prosecute company officers and even have powers to prosecute employees if they wilfully contribute to environmental harm.

questions.prompt: Which of the following work procedures on electrical systems will always require a permit-to-work to be issued?
questions.explanation: An electrical permit-to-work should state what circuit or equipment has been made safe, how that has been achieved and what work is to be done. A permit should not, therefore, be used for live working. Such a permit is always required for work on high-voltage systems, but can also be used for low-voltage systems.

questions.prompt: The use of a multi-lock hasp with the appropriate number of padlocks is a recommended method of safe isolation where:

options.A: Individual circuit breaker locking off devices are not available
options.B: Individual circuit breakers are not identified at the distribution board
options.C: More than one person will be working on circuits supplied from the same distribution board
options.D: You know the health and safety inspector is in the area

questions.explanation: When several people work on circuits from one board, each fits their own padlock to the hasp so the isolator cannot be switched back on until everyone has finished and removed their lock. This guarantees no one re-energises the supply while another worker is still exposed.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is classed as hazardous/special waste?
questions.explanation: Hazardous wastes (special wastes in Scotland) are specified in waste legislation. Fluorescent tubes are included because of their mercury content.

questions.prompt: What colour cable USUALLY signifies 110 volt power supply on site?
questions.explanation: Yellow is the recognised site colour for 110 V reduced low voltage equipment, used on cables, plugs, sockets and transformers. The colour lets workers instantly identify the safer 110 V centre-tapped supply and distinguish it from 230 V blue equipment.

questions.prompt: The probes of voltage detectors and test instruments used on electrical systems should be:

options.D: Shaped or have barriers to prevent finger contact with the tips

questions.explanation: In addition, to protect against damage by overcurrent whilst in use, the probes or instrument should incorporate suitable high breaking capacity (hbc) fuses with a low current rating (usually not exceeding 500 mA), or current-limiting resistors.

questions.prompt: A mobile plant operator can let you ride in the machine:

options.B: If it is designed to carry passengers
options.D: If you have a long way to go

questions.explanation: You may only ride in mobile plant that is purpose-built with a proper passenger seat. Climbing onto machines not designed to carry people risks falls, crushing or being struck by moving parts, so it is forbidden however convenient it seems.

questions.prompt: Test instruments used for working on electrical systems should:
questions.explanation: To protect the user from electric shock whilst using the instrument, i.e. handling the probes.

questions.prompt: To prove a circuit or equipment is dead after isolation what is the FIRST activity in the sequence of events?

options.C: Check that the voltage detector is working on a proving device, known live source or in- built test feature
options.D: Make sure equipment is not working

questions.explanation: This will prove that that the voltage detector (such as a two-pole voltage detector or proprietary test lamp) is working, i.e. indicating voltage.

questions.prompt: What must be considered first when planning to carry out work in a confined space?

options.A: Can the work be done from the outside
options.C: Has the job been priced properly
options.D: Have the correct tools been arranged

questions.explanation: Working outside will remove the risks of working in the confined space.

questions.prompt: While digging a trench, you uncover a length of yellow marker tape at a depth of about 150mm. What does the presence of the marker tape mean?

options.A: The area has a high water-table and precautions must be taken to prevent an in-rush of water
options.B: The excavation has reached a depth where the sides must now be supported
options.C: There is a buried electrical cable and further excavation must be carried out with care
options.D: There is contaminated soil below the level of the marker tape and all excavation must stop

questions.explanation: The coloured tape indicates that there are buried services below the route of the tape.

questions.prompt: How often should user (visual) checks be carried out on portable electrical equipment?
questions.explanation: All items of portable electrical equipment should be visually checked for safety by the user before being put into use.

questions.prompt: If you are about to use a power tool and discover the guard is missing, you should:

options.A: Make up a temporary guard yourself
options.B: Not use the tool until a proper guard has been fitted
options.C: Use the tool but try to work quickly
options.D: Use the tool but work carefully and slowly

questions.explanation: Visual checks should be carried out before using equipment. Any faults should be reported immediately and rectified before use.

questions.prompt: What is the best method of securing a ladder?

options.B: Tying it to a suitable point
options.C: Using an effective ladder stability device
options.D: Wedging the ladder (eg against a wall)

questions.explanation: Tying the ladder is the safest option, making sure both stiles are tied.

questions.prompt: The electric drill you are about to use has a faulty on/off switch. What action should you take?

options.A: Find another machine and carry on working
options.B: Stop work and inform your supervisor
options.C: Tape the switch on to keep it running and carry on working

questions.explanation: A faulty on/off switch means the tool cannot be reliably controlled or stopped, which is dangerous. You should stop, take it out of use and report it so it can be repaired or replaced; you must never bodge or keep using defective equipment.

questions.prompt: When should visual checks of portable hand-held equipment be made by the user?
questions.explanation: The user needs to be satisfied that the tool has no obvious defect before use.

questions.prompt: A working platform used for construction work, and from which a person could fall 2 metres or more, must not be used unless it has been inspected (and a report is subsequently prepared) by a competent person:
questions.explanation: Under these specific circumstances a report is required to be prepared by the competent person and given to the person for whom the inspection was done (e.g. the site manager). This is in addition to the more general requirement to inspect equipment for work at height: prior to use in that position (or site if it is mobile); following exceptional circumstances (e.g. high winds); and at suitable intervals.

questions.prompt: When working on fragile roofs:

options.A: As long as you avoid any fragile areas it is safe
options.B: Crawling boards should always be used
options.C: It is safe to walk on the purlins
options.D: Walk straight across the roof to where you need to get to

questions.explanation: Fragile roofs must be made safe to work on, before work commences.

questions.prompt: In an emergency situation at work you should do what?

options.A: Ensure your work mates are all accounted for

questions.explanation: A site emergency plan should have been drawn up and you should be familiar with the emergency procedure.

questions.prompt: What does the sound of a siren on-site normally indicate?
questions.explanation: A site siren is the general alarm signalling an emergency that requires everyone to respond, usually by evacuating to the assembly point. It is not specific to one hazard, so you treat any siren as a call to leave the area immediately.

questions.prompt: Most deaths on site are caused by:
questions.explanation: Although the other dangers can kill or cause injury, falling from height is the bigger cause of fatalities.

questions.prompt: The rung of a wooden ladder has started to split, what should you do?

options.B: Do not use it, tell your supervisor
options.C: Jump on it to see if it holds your weight

questions.explanation: A split rung can give way under load and cause a serious fall, so the ladder must be taken out of use and reported. Taping or cutting it does not restore its strength, and testing it by standing on it risks injury.

questions.prompt: A red-labelled fire extinguisher should NOT be used:

options.D: Where there is a risk of electrocution

questions.explanation: Red denotes water. Liquids should not be used on electrical fires, since they can conduct electricity.

questions.prompt: In an on-site emergency, which of the following must a first-aider NOT do?

options.B: Give medicines to patients without authorization

questions.explanation: First-aid is concerned with preserving life and limb, and first-aiders are not trained to dispense medical treatments.

questions.prompt: A workmate lifting a big box suddenly shouts "oh, my back" and drops the box. What should you do?

options.A: Find them somewhere comfortable to sit and rest
options.B: Help them to lift the box
options.D: Tell them to leave it for someone else to lift

questions.explanation: The priority for any back injury is to obtain first-aid advice, in order to prevent further damage.

questions.prompt: Which fire extinguisher should not be used on flammable liquid fires?
questions.explanation: Water must never be used on flammable liquid fires because the burning liquid floats on the water and is spread around, enlarging the fire. Foam, CO2 or powder smother the flames and cut off oxygen, which is why they are suitable instead.

questions.prompt: If you discover a fire at work, what should you do first:

options.A: Raise the alarm and warn fellow workers
options.B: Run around looking for an alarm to sound
options.D: Use a fire extinguisher to put it out

questions.explanation: Raising the alarm will reduce the risk to others, particularly if the fire spreads.

questions.prompt: Excessive sunlight on bare skin can cause which serious health problem?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet rays in sunlight can cause sunburn and premature ageing of the skin. The most serious effect, however, is an increased chance of developing skin cancer.

questions.prompt: Asbestos is suspected in the workplace, during renovation do you:
questions.explanation: Competent advice must be sought, to prevent exposure to the worker or others, either at the time, or subsequently.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not required to be provided under the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations?
questions.explanation: Guidance on the provision of welfare facilities as required by CDM is given in HSE publication 'Health and Safety in Construction'.

questions.prompt: A colleague has drilled holes in the top of his safety helmet because the weather is hot. Is this:

options.B: Acceptable if the holes are small

questions.explanation: Interfering with or misusing items provided in the interests of health, safety or welfare is an offence under the HSW Act 1974 (section 8).

questions.prompt: Why should a high visibility vest be worn when working on roads?

options.A: Because it will keep you warm
options.B: Because you were told to do so
options.C: So road users and plant operators can see you
options.D: So that your mates can see you

questions.explanation: So road users and plant operators can see you is correct because site transport and plant risks are controlled by separation, competence, visibility, and following the planned system of work. The chosen option reduces the chance of being struck or crushed.

questions.prompt: If you are drilling into concrete with a masonry drill, in which one of the following circumstances will you need to wear eye protection?

options.B: Not if drilling into the floor
options.C: Only if the drill is bigger than 10mm

questions.explanation: Suitable eye protection must always be worn when working with power-driven tools where chippings are likely to fly or abrasive materials could be propelled.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to report 'near miss' accidents to your employer?

options.B: So lessons can be learned, preventing an accident next time
options.C: So that someone can be disciplined
options.D: To make the figures look good

questions.explanation: The HSE advises that 'near misses' should be investigated to prevent their recurrence.

questions.prompt: When working in dusty conditions, what of the following would give the LEAST level of protection?
questions.explanation: Protection factors are given in HSE publication HSG53 'Respiratory protective equipment at work - A practical guide'

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is classified as a reportable occupational disease under RIDDOR?
questions.explanation: Certain occupational diseases likely to have been caused or made worse by work are reportable under RIDDOR. This would include occupational asthma where the person's work includes significant or regular exposure to a known respiratory sensitizer.

questions.prompt: When picking up an object, you should:
questions.explanation: Generally, the legs should do most of the work when lifting a load.

questions.prompt: Which would you consider to be generally correct when lifting a load?

options.A: Keep the load away from the body
options.B: Larger loads should be split into smaller loads if possible
options.C: The feet should be together and the load lifted at arm's length
options.D: When lifting you should bend your back

questions.explanation: Splitting a large load into smaller, more manageable loads reduces the weight handled at one time and the strain on the back. Keeping loads close to the body, feet apart and the back straight are the correct techniques, which the other options reverse.

questions.prompt: Under RIDDOR, which one of the following must be reported to the enforcing authority?

options.A: Accidents where the injured person wishes to make a claim
options.B: All 'near misses' even if no one is hurt
options.D: Fracture other than to fingers, thumbs or toes

questions.explanation: This is one of a number of reportable 'specified injuries' and must be reported to the enforcing authority under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR).

questions.prompt: What would you NOT consider in making a judgement of the risks from a load?
questions.explanation: A, C and D can all affect the difficulty of lifting an object.

questions.prompt: In manual handling, which of the following general statements is true?

options.A: Anyone can carry any load as long as they are strong enough
options.B: Large loads should be broken down into smaller loads where possible
options.C: Loads should be held at arm's length while carrying
options.D: You should keep your back bent when lifting

questions.explanation: Breaking a large load into smaller portions lowers the weight lifted in one go, reducing the risk of back and muscle injury. Carrying at arm's length or with a bent back increases strain, and capacity depends on the person and load, not just strength.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations require the colour coding of safety signs. What colours are used on a sign indicating a prohibited activity, for example "No access for pedestrians"?
questions.explanation: Prohibitory signs are round and feature a black pictogram on a white background with red edging and diagonal line.

questions.prompt: Under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, which of the following have a duty to work safely?
questions.explanation: Employers, employees and the self-employed all have duties to work safely under the Act.

questions.prompt: What do the letters ACoP stand for?
questions.explanation: An ACOP is a code of practice approved by the Health and Safety Executive (or the Health and Safety Commission prior to April 2008).

questions.prompt: Complete the following sentence: A risk assessment

options.A: Is a means of analysing what might go wrong
options.B: Is a piece of paper required by law

questions.explanation: Risk assessment involves a careful review of what can cause harm and the practical measures to be taken to reduce the risk of harm.

questions.prompt: Who is responsible for signing a Company Safety Policy?
questions.explanation: The Health and Safety at Work Act requires the most senior member of management to sign the health and safety policy statement.

questions.prompt: Identify one method of enforcing regulations that are available to the Health and Safety Executive:
questions.explanation: An Improvement Notice is a formal HSE enforcement tool requiring a duty holder to correct a breach of health and safety law within a set time. It is one of the statutory powers inspectors hold, alongside the Prohibition Notice that stops dangerous activity at once.

questions.prompt: If you discover a hole or gap in a fire rated wall or floor that has not been fire-stopped, what should you do?

options.A: Cover the hole or gap with insulating tape
options.B: Use decorators' sealant to fill the gap
options.C: Ignore it unless it is causing a draught
options.D: Report it to your supervisor without delay

questions.explanation: Reference: Supervisors need to be made aware of any observed inadequacies in fire-stopping - which can undermine fire precautions catastrophically during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

questions.prompt: In addition to preserving fire separation between areas of a building, which other important fire safety function can fire-stopping achieve?
questions.explanation: Reference: During the fire, it is essential that the load-bearing capacity of elements of the building structure are maintained until the occupants have escaped. Timber studs, joists or 'I' beams, for example, may only have a short survival time if exposed to fire and may rely on linings, such as plasterboard ceiling, for fire resistance. Services passing through such linings should therefore be fire-stopped.

questions.prompt: Intumescent materials used to provide fire-stopping are designed to:
questions.explanation: Reference: A limited number of fire-resistant materials may be used to provide fire-stopping. These include intumescent products, which are designed to expand and provide fire-stopping when subjected to heat. Examples include intumescent 'pillows' (used to provide internal sealing of trunking) and intumescent mastic.

questions.prompt: The purpose of fire-stopping in a building is to:

options.C: Delay the passage of fire and smoke through openings in walls and floors

questions.explanation: Reference: Fire-stopping is a passive fire protection measure used to seal any openings created in a fire resistance-rated wall or floor assembly, e.g. to allow pipes or wiring systems to pass through. During fire conditions this will impede the spread of fire and smoke.

questions.prompt: What are fire-stops designed to do?

options.B: Protect services (such as wiring systems) against fire damage
options.D: Delay the passage of fire and smoke through openings in walls and floors

questions.explanation: Reference: Fire-stops are designed to maintain the fireproofing of a wall or floor assembly. Fire-stopping delays the spread of fire and, generally, the spread of smoke as well.

questions.prompt: When storing liquids (such as oils, fuels or chemicals) on-site, what must you do?

options.A: Keep the tops off, to prevent pressure from building up
options.B: Ensure the liquid material is stored safely and securely, and out of the way of site traffic
options.C: Use a transparent container so you can check how much liquid is in it

questions.explanation: Reference: Any spillage could get into the ground or drains, which is likely to be an offence under environmental legislation.

questions.prompt: From an environmental point of view, why should materials be reused, where possible?

options.C: A lot of energy and raw materials go into making most construction products
options.D: It makes less mess on site

questions.explanation: Reference: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the re-use of materials can also contribute to effective waste management.

questions.prompt: If you have unused material left, what should you do before you consider putting non-hazardous waste items into a skip?

options.A: Put it in a plastic bag and put it in a skip
options.C: Make sure there is a label on it
options.D: Check whether someone else on your team can make use of it

questions.explanation: Reference: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the reuse of waste materials is much better than disposal, which is the most expensive option and which should be the last resort. Reuse is a better waste management option than recovery.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a suitable means of isolating a circuit?

options.A: Fitting a padlocked circuit breaker lockout
options.B: Removing a fuse and locking the distribution board
options.D: Putting insulating tape over the circuit breaker

questions.explanation: Reference: The isolating device should be switched off or the fuse removed. The switch, circuit breaker or enclosure should then be locked and the key removed. A notice or label should also be posted to warn that someone is working on the circuit or apparatus.

questions.prompt: What colour cable USUALLY signifies 110 volt power supply on site?
questions.explanation: Reference: Yellow is the usual colour of cables, socket outlets, plugs and transformers etc which are used with a 110 volt supply.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true with regard to the dangers of electricity?

options.A: Electricity is only dangerous if you are not wearing wellington boots
options.B: Electricity is dangerous at any time because you cannot tell by looking at a cable whether or not it is live
options.C: Electricity is only dangerous in wet weather
options.D: Electricity is perfectly safe so long as you wear cotton gloves

questions.explanation: Reference: The features which make electricity so dangerous are that you cannot see, hear or smell it. It can give you a very unpleasant surprise. Always assume that cables are live.

questions.prompt: Test instruments used for working on electrical systems should:
questions.explanation: Reference: To protect the user from electric shock whilst using the instrument, i.e. handling the probes.

questions.prompt: When is live working permissible?

options.A: When it is unreasonable in all circumstances for the equipment to be made dead and suitable precautions are taken
options.B: When the person carrying out the work is a competent person
options.C: When the person working on the equipment is wearing rubber gloves
options.D: When the means of isolation cannot be identified

questions.explanation: Reference: This is a requirement under r.14 of the EAW Regulations. However, it does not mean that live working is then 'safe'

questions.prompt: The lowest level of electrical current which can harm the human body is normally measured in:
questions.explanation: Reference: Research has shown that a person is in serious danger of a fatal electric shock at, or above, approximately 30 milliamps.

questions.prompt: What must be considered first when planning to carry out work in a confined space?

options.B: Can the work be done from the outside
options.C: Has the job been priced properly
options.D: Have the correct tools been arranged

questions.explanation: Reference: Working outside will remove the risks of working in the confined space.

questions.prompt: While digging a trench, you uncover a length of yellow marker tape at a depth of about 150mm. What does the presence of the marker tape mean?

options.A: There is contaminated soil below the level of the marker tape and all excavation must stop
options.B: The area has a high water-table and precautions must be taken to prevent an in-rush of water
options.C: There is a buried electrical cable and further excavation must be carried out with care
options.D: The excavation has reached a depth where the sides must now be supported

questions.explanation: Reference: The coloured tape indicates that there are buried services below the route of the tape.

questions.prompt: When do special precautions need to be taken when working near overhead electric power lines?

options.A: Only if plant has to pass under the lines
options.B: Only if cranes etc. are being used
options.C: Only if someone could touch a line with their bare hands
options.D: Whenever work areas will be near or beneath the lines

questions.explanation: Reference: Actual contact with a power line is not necessary to result in an electric shock as a close approach may allow 'flashover' to occur. HSE publication GS6 gives advice on procedures to avoid such danger.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred nominal voltage for portable hand tools on construction sites?
questions.explanation: Reference: 110 volt reduced low voltage systems are strongly preferred for the supply to such equipment.

questions.prompt: Who should operate plant and equipment on site?

options.C: An employee holding a full driving license
options.D: Only people over 18 years of age

questions.explanation: Reference: Never operate plant or equipment unless you have been trained and are authorised to do so.

questions.prompt: The electric drill you are about to use has a faulty on/off switch. What action should you take?

options.A: Find another machine and carry on working
options.B: Tape the switch on to keep it running and carry on working
options.C: Stop work and inform your supervisor

questions.explanation: Reference: It is essential that supervisors are aware of faulty or damaged equipment.

questions.prompt: What precaution should you take before adjusting an electrical tool?

options.A: Wear the correct personal protective equipment
options.B: Check the lead is not twisted or knotted
options.D: Wear safety footwear with steel toecaps

questions.explanation: Reference: Do not adjust tools which could still be live or operate.

questions.prompt: When can you work from a ladder?

options.A: When not being used for access
options.B: For short periods and then only if it is safe to do so

questions.explanation: Reference: Ladders are primarily means of access, not workplaces. They can be worked from, but only if the use of other, more suitable, work equipment is not appropriate and the task is of low risk and of short duration.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum height of the top guard-rail of a scaffold above the edge from which someone is liable to fall?
questions.explanation: Reference: This is a requirement of the Work at Height Regulations 2005.

questions.prompt: If you have to work at height and it is not possible to erect a scaffold, or use any other type of working platform or mobile elevating work platform, then you should:

options.A: Wear a harness and lanyard at all times
options.B: Work without fall protection at all times when no one else is about
options.C: Work without fall protection, provided you have a mate with you
options.D: Work without fall protection, provided the weather is not too windy

questions.explanation: Reference: The harness will greatly reduce the likelihood of injury if you fall.

questions.prompt: Half the deaths on construction sites are caused by which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Falls from height are the single biggest cause of fatal accidents in construction, accounting for around half of deaths. This is why work at height must be properly planned with guarding, secure access and fall protection rather than improvised access.

questions.prompt: What is the ideal angle for a ladder against a wall and floor?

options.A: One metre up for every metre out from the wall
options.B: Two metres up for every metre out from the wall
options.C: Four metres up for every metre out from the wall
options.D: One metre up for every two metres out from the wall

questions.explanation: Reference: The correct angle for a ladder is 75 degrees, which an be judged using the angle indicator marked on the stiles of some ladders or using the 1 in 4 rule.

questions.prompt: A workmate burns their hand on a piece of very hot metal. What should you do first?

options.A: Warn other people about the piece of hot metal
options.B: Cover the burn with something dry
options.C: Put their hand in cold water if it is available
options.D: Rub some cream or Vaseline into the burn

questions.explanation: Cooling the burn with running cold water removes heat from the tissue, limiting how deep the damage spreads and easing pain. Creams or Vaseline trap heat and risk infection, and a dry dressing comes only after cooling.

questions.prompt: In an on-site emergency, which of the following must a first-aider NOT do?

options.C: Give medicines to patients without authorization

questions.explanation: Reference: First-aid is concerned with preserving life and limb, and first-aiders are not trained to dispense medical treatments.

questions.prompt: What action should you take if you discover a fire?

options.A: Leave it because you will get the blame
options.C: Extinguish the fire without raising the alarm
options.D: Carry on working if it is safe to do so

questions.explanation: Reference: Raising the alarm will reduce the risk to others, particularly if the fire spreads.

questions.prompt: Which of the following animals can carry Weil's disease?
questions.explanation: Reference: Weil's disease is a serious and sometimes fatal infection that can be transmitted to humans by contact with infected rats. Another form of Leptospirosis infection can be transmitted from cattle to humans.

questions.prompt: While working you discover material you think could be asbestos. What should you do?

options.B: Clear any dust and fragments, put them in a bin then carry on working
options.C: Dampen the material to prevent further dust being created, then carry on working
options.D: Stop working immediately and report your suspicions to your supervisor

questions.explanation: Reference: It is essential to stop work if asbestos is found or suspected, and await competent advice on what to do next.

questions.prompt: If you have been handling lead, how is it most likely to get into your blood stream?

options.A: By not reporting the matter to the HSE
options.B: By not using the correct safety footwear
options.C: By not washing your hands before eating

questions.explanation: Reference: The route into the body is ingestion, normally from lead contamination on the hands.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following must apply to any hard hat provided?

options.A: It is less than 1 year old
options.C: It is less than 2 years old
options.D: It is less than 5 years old

questions.explanation: Reference: All PPE should be CE - marked, indicating that it meets the basic health and safety requirements.

questions.prompt: Why should a high visibility vest be worn when working on roads?

options.A: So road users and plant operators can see you
options.B: So that your mates can see you
options.C: Because you were told to do so
options.D: Because it will keep you warm

questions.explanation: Reference: Many workers are struck and injured, often seriously, by moving vehicles.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following should you do if your personal protective equipment (PPE) is damaged?

options.C: Reduce the amount of time you use it
options.D: Report to your Supervisor without delay

questions.explanation: Reference: Employees are required to report any defective PPE to their employer (PPE at Work Regulations 1992, Regulation 7)

questions.prompt: Which of the following must your safety helmet comply with to meet with the requirements of the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations?

options.A: It is a good visible colour
options.B: It has a label with your name on it
options.C: It can be adjusted to suit your head size
options.D: It is less than 1 year old

questions.explanation: Reference: An assessment of the suitability of head protection would include consideration of whether it can be adjusted to suit the individual who is to wear it, that it is compatible with the work to be done and that it is comfortable to wear.

questions.prompt: Under which of the following circumstances should an accident be recorded in the site's accident book?

options.A: When an accident causes damage to plant or equipment
options.B: When the injury is serious enough for first aid to be needed.
options.C: When an accident causes injury to an employee while at work
options.D: Only when a person is injured and will be off work for more than seven days

questions.explanation: Reference: An accident causing an injury to an employee at work should be recorded in the accident book (BI 510).

questions.prompt: When judging "individual capability" for manual handling, you should assume:
questions.explanation: Reference: Assessing ability for manual handling must be done on an individual basis.
