questions.prompt: Why should a serious accident be reported to the enforcing authority?

options.A: So that the site manager can see who is to blame
options.B: So that the company will be held responsible
options.C: It helps the site find out what caused it

questions.explanation: Reference: Serious accidents (specified injuries or those resulting in an absence of over 7 days) must be reported to the enforcing authority under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR).

questions.prompt: Under RIDDOR, which one of the following must be reported to the enforcing authority?

options.A: Fracture other than to fingers, thumbs or toes
options.B: All 'near misses' even if no one is hurt
options.D: Accidents where the injured person wishes to make a claim

questions.explanation: Reference: This is one of a number of reportable 'specified injuries' and must be reported to the enforcing authority under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR).

questions.prompt: What is the most common type of injury resulting from lifting loads from the floor?
questions.explanation: Lifting from floor level forces you to bend and put strain on the spine, so the back is by far the most commonly injured area. Poor technique and twisting under load make muscle and disc damage very likely.

questions.prompt: What is the recommended limit for a compact load that can be safely carried by a fit, male worker?
questions.explanation: Reference: This figure is in HSE guidance, and relates to lifting and lowering at elbow height.

questions.prompt: If there is a risk of injury from moving loads what should you think about?

options.D: Getting someone to assist you over the distance

questions.explanation: Reference: This is a requirement of the Manual Handling Operations regulations 1992.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations require the colour coding of safety signs. What colours are used on a sign indicating a mandatory activity, for example "Safety helmets must be worn"?
questions.explanation: Mandatory signs that tell you what you must do, like wearing a helmet, are a blue circle with a white symbol. Red means prohibition or fire, yellow with black warns of a hazard, and green indicates safe conditions or escape routes.

questions.prompt: Why should regular inspections of the workplace take place?

options.A: To check that all employees are present
options.B: To check that everyone is doing their job
options.C: To check whether the working environment is safe
options.D: To prepare for a visit from an HSE Inspector

questions.explanation: Reference: The Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations require that routine inspections of workplaces are carried out to ensure that preventative and protective measures are in place and effective.

questions.prompt: What is the MAXIMUM penalty that a Higher Court, can currently impose for a breach of the Health and Safety at Work Act?

options.B: Unlimited fine and two years imprisonment

questions.explanation: Reference: A Lower Court can impose a fine of up to £20,000 and/or up to six months imprisonment for certain offences. The potential fine in a Higher Court, however, is unlimited and the term of imprisonment can be up to 2 years.

questions.prompt: Regulations that govern health and safety on construction sites:

options.A: Do not apply during 'out of hours' working

questions.explanation: Reference: The requirements of health and safety law are mandatory, and failure to follow them can lead to prosecutions.

questions.prompt: What is a HAZARD?

options.B: The likelihood of something going wrong
options.C: Something with the potential to cause harm
options.D: Where an accident is likely to happen

questions.explanation: Reference: Examples of hazards include: a drum of acid, breeze blocks on an elevated plank; cables running across a floor.

questions.prompt: A Prohibition Notice means:

options.A: When you finish the work you must not start again
options.C: Work may continue until the end of the day
options.D: Work is to stop for that day only

questions.explanation: Reference: The work activity covered by the prohibition notice must cease, until the identified danger is removed.

questions.prompt: The Electricity at Work Regulations require that:

options.A: A training course is necessary before anyone can work with electricity
options.B: Anyone supervised can work with electricity
options.C: Only electricians can work with electricity
options.D: Persons working with electricity must have the appropriate level of knowledge and experience

questions.explanation: The Regulations require electrical work to be done only by people competent for the task, meaning they hold suitable knowledge and experience for the danger involved. Competence, not a single course or job title, is what keeps work safe.

questions.prompt: The Electricity at Work Regulations apply to:
questions.explanation: The EAW Regulations cover the safe use of electricity in work activities, irrespective of voltage.

questions.prompt: Which of the following should be used to prove a circuit or equipment is dead after isolation?

options.A: A lamp holder with a length of flex attached
options.C: A proprietary test lamp or two-pole voltage detector

questions.explanation: Accident history has shown that using incorrectly set multimeters or makeshift devices for voltage detection has often caused accidents. The use of non-contact voltage indicators (voltage sticks) is also not advised as the sole means of proving dead.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a suitable means of isolating a circuit?

options.A: Fitting a padlocked circuit breaker lockout
options.C: Putting insulating tape over the circuit breaker
options.D: Removing a fuse and locking the distribution board

questions.explanation: The isolating device should be switched off or the fuse removed. The switch, circuit breaker or enclosure should then be locked and the key removed. A notice or label should also be posted to warn that someone is working on the circuit or apparatus.

questions.prompt: Which of the following work procedures on electrical systems will always require a permit-to-work to be issued?
questions.explanation: An electrical permit-to-work should state what circuit or equipment has been made safe, how that has been achieved and what work is to be done. A permit should not, therefore, be used for live working. Such a permit is always required for work on high-voltage systems, but can also be used for low-voltage systems.

questions.prompt: Optical fibre cable remnants should not be left lying around on site because:

options.A: Laser beams still exist in the cut pieces
options.C: They can be hot and burn upon contact
options.D: They can pierce the skin or eyes

questions.explanation: Fibre fragments can enter the bloodstream and cause infections in the skin or eyes. All fibre waste, particularly small pieces, should be placed in suitable receptacles.

questions.prompt: Why should the end of an optical fibre cable never be pointed towards your own or anyone else's eyes?

options.A: The beam can bore a hole through the skin
options.B: The beam can damage the eyes
options.C: The beam can transfer a strong electric current
options.D: The colour of the beam is very hypnotic

questions.explanation: Exposure to light sources such as lasers or highly concentrated visible or infrared light beams, associated with the testing or use of optical fibres, can cause damage to the eyes, or even blindness.

questions.prompt: The use of a multi-lock hasp with the appropriate number of padlocks is a recommended method of safe isolation where:

options.A: Individual circuit breaker locking off devices are not available
options.B: Individual circuit breakers are not identified at the distribution board
options.C: More than one person will be working on circuits supplied from the same distribution board
options.D: You know the health and safety inspector is in the area

questions.explanation: A multi-lock hasp lets several workers each fit their own padlock, so the isolator cannot be switched back on until every person has finished and removed their lock. This guarantees no one is re-energised while another is still working.

questions.prompt: Which of the following procedures should be used when more than one person will be working on circuits supplied from a distribution board which has been switched off?

options.A: Blowing a horn before the power is switched on again
options.B: Giving each operative a volt stick
options.C: Telling everyone what time the power will be switched on again
options.D: The use of a multi-lock hasp on the isolator with a padlock for each operative

questions.explanation: With several people working from one isolated board, each fits a padlock to a multi-lock hasp so the supply stays off until everyone has finished and removed their own lock. Verbal warnings or horns rely on memory and cannot physically prevent re-energisation.

questions.prompt: What colour cable USUALLY signifies 110 volt power supply on site?
questions.explanation: Reduced low-voltage 110V site supplies are colour-coded yellow across cables, plugs, sockets and transformers so they are instantly recognisable. The 110V centre-tapped system limits shock voltage to around 55V to earth, making it safer for site tools.

questions.prompt: A portable electric generator on site has two power outlets, 110 volts and 230 volts. What colour would the 110 volt outlet be?
questions.explanation: The 110V outlet is yellow, matching the standard colour code for reduced low-voltage site equipment. Blue is used for 230V supplies, so the distinct colours stop tools being plugged into the wrong, more dangerous voltage.

questions.prompt: Where there is no local means of isolation for equipment or circuits to be worked on, which of the following is the preferred method of isolation?

options.A: Disconnecting the individual circuit from the DB
options.B: Isolation of the individual circuit breaker or fuse
options.C: Isolation of the main switch or DB switch- disconnector
options.D: Pulling out the distributor's cut-out fuse

questions.explanation: Without a local isolator, you isolate at the main switch or board switch-disconnector, which is designed to safely break the supply on load and can be locked off. Pulling the supplier's cut-out fuse is not yours to touch, and unbolting a circuit live is unsafe.

questions.prompt: What action should you take if a workmate gets an electric shock?

options.A: Cut off the power and call for help
options.B: Dial 999 and ask for the fire brigade
options.D: Try to pull them to safety

questions.explanation: If you can switch the power off, the electric hazard will be removed. First aid assistance will then probably be required. Do not touch someone who is still in contact with live electrical cables as you could also receive an electric shock.

questions.prompt: A residual current device is designed to operate in the event of one of the following:
questions.explanation: An RCD detects an imbalance between line and neutral currents, which occurs when current leaks to earth, and trips quickly to protect against electric shock. Overloads and short-circuits are handled by fuses or MCBs, not the RCD.

questions.prompt: Electrical installations on construction sites should be periodically inspected and tested:
questions.explanation: Three monthly inspections of construction site installations are recommended in IEE Guidance Note 3.

questions.prompt: The maximum AC voltage which the human body can withstand without long term physiological effects in dry conditions is:
questions.explanation: 50 volts is correct because electrical safety depends on preventing contact with live parts, using the right supply/protection, and taking damaged equipment out of service. Isolation or reporting beats continuing with an unsafe tool.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true with regard to the dangers of electricity?

options.A: Electricity is dangerous at any time because you cannot tell by looking at a cable whether or not it is live
options.B: Electricity is only dangerous if you are not wearing wellington boots
options.C: Electricity is only dangerous in wet weather
options.D: Electricity is perfectly safe so long as you wear cotton gloves

questions.explanation: The features which make electricity so dangerous are that you cannot see, hear or smell it. It can give you a very unpleasant surprise. Always assume that cables are live.

questions.prompt: What is the most serious effect that electric shock can have if you come into contact with a live part?

options.A: The electric current can cause a slight tingling in the fingers
options.B: The electric current can cause burn marks on the fingers
options.C: The electric current can cause the finger muscles to twitch
options.D: The electric current can cause the heart to stop, resulting in death

questions.explanation: Contact with live electrical parts can be fatal. If you do not know otherwise, always assume that electrical parts are live.

questions.prompt: Your job involves you working near to hanging electrical cables which have bare ends. What should you do?

options.A: Attempt to push the cables back into the ceiling void so that you can start work
options.B: Carry on working, as there shouldn't be a problem
options.C: Inform your supervisor and keep well away
options.D: Touch the cables to see if they are live

questions.explanation: You must always assume that exposed cables are live until you know they are not. Contact with live electrical cables can kill.

questions.prompt: For all live working activities it is necessary to:

options.B: Carry out a risk assessment as required by the EAW Regulations.

questions.explanation: Live work is only justified when unavoidable, and the Electricity at Work Regulations require a risk assessment to confirm it is reasonable and to set the precautions needed. This drives the decision on accompaniment, PPE and any other controls.

questions.prompt: An electrical Permit to Work is primarily a statement that:

options.A: Certain instructions need to be followed
options.B: Someone else has taken responsibility for the work
options.C: The circuit or equipment has been isolated and is safe to work on
options.D: The circuit or equipment is live

questions.explanation: Permits to work describe the procedures that prevent a major hazard, such as electricity or moving machinery, from causing harm, usually by isolation to effectively ensure (in the case of electricity) 'dead' working with no chance of it going 'live'.

questions.prompt: The probes of voltage detectors and test instruments used on electrical systems should be:

options.D: Shaped or have barriers to prevent finger contact with the tips

questions.explanation: In addition, to protect against damage by overcurrent whilst in use, the probes or instrument should incorporate suitable high breaking capacity (hbc) fuses with a low current rating (usually not exceeding 500 mA), or current-limiting resistors.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does the Electricity at Work (EAW) regulations apply to?

options.A: All persons engaged for work purposes

questions.explanation: The EAW Regulations impose duties on employers, employees and the self employed.

questions.prompt: In accordance with the Electricity at Work regulations, when considering whether to work live a responsible person should:
questions.explanation: To identify and assess the risks involved and the methods of controlling them.

questions.prompt: The normal procedure for working on electrical equipment should be which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Dead working should be considered as the norm and work on or near live conductors should rarely be permitted

questions.prompt: Test instruments used for working on electrical systems should:
questions.explanation: To protect the user from electric shock whilst using the instrument, i.e. handling the probes.

questions.prompt: Under the Electricity at Work Regulations, live working is considered:

options.C: Only to be allowed in exceptional circumstances

questions.explanation: Extra controls must be employed, including training, supervision and use of suitable tools and protective equipment.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would you use to replace the fuse in a plug if fuses were NOT available?
questions.explanation: A fuse is often the main safety device in an electrical circuit. A blown fuse must only be replaced by a fuse of the correct type and rating.

questions.prompt: To prove a circuit or equipment is dead after isolation what is the FIRST activity in the sequence of events?

options.C: Check that the voltage detector is working on a proving device, known live source or in- built test feature
options.D: Make sure equipment is not working

questions.explanation: This will prove that that the voltage detector (such as a two-pole voltage detector or proprietary test lamp) is working, i.e. indicating voltage.

questions.prompt: The nominal single phase voltage in the UK is?
questions.explanation: This is the nominal voltage for public electricity supply systems within Europe.

questions.prompt: When is live working permissible?

options.A: When it is unreasonable in all circumstances for the equipment to be made dead and suitable precautions are taken
options.B: When the means of isolation cannot be identified
options.C: When the person carrying out the work is a competent person
options.D: When the person working on the equipment is wearing rubber gloves

questions.explanation: This is a requirement under r.14 of the EAW Regulations. However, it does not mean that live working is then 'safe'

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a requirement of low voltage safe isolation practice?

options.A: A caution notice should be applied at the point of isolation
options.B: Ensuring that the correct point of isolation is identified
options.C: The conductors are proved to be dead at the point of work
options.D: The person carrying out the work is issued with insulating gloves

questions.explanation: Safe isolation practice refers to dead working. The use of insulating gloves will generally only be applicable to live working.

questions.prompt: The specific effects on the human body of a major electric shock are one of the following:
questions.explanation: A major electric shock drives current through the body, causing deep burns where it enters and exits and disrupting the heart's rhythm, leading to cardiac arrest. These are the immediate life-threatening effects, unlike chest pains or dermatitis.

questions.prompt: The lowest level of electrical current which can harm the human body is normally measured in:
questions.explanation: Research has shown that a person is in serious danger of a fatal electric shock at, or above, approximately 30 milliamps.

questions.prompt: With regard to the effect of electrical current on the human body, one of the following is correct:

options.A: A 3 amp fuse should prevent a person receiving a fatal electric shock
options.B: A 30mA Residual Current Device (RCD) should prevent a person receiving a fatal electric shock.
options.C: A 5 amp rewireable fuse should prevent a person receiving a fatal electric shock
options.D: A 6 amp circuit breaker should prevent a person receiving a fatal electric shock

questions.explanation: An RCD is a mechanical switching device intended to cause the opening of the contacts when the residual current attains a given value under specified conditions.

questions.prompt: Where mains voltage is used to supply portable equipment on a construction site, what additional protection is required?
questions.explanation: Reduced low voltage systems (e.g. 110 volt centre point earthed) are strongly preferred in such circumstances. Where only mains voltage (230 V) equipment is available, however, a 30 mA RCD will give additional protection against fatal electric shock.

questions.prompt: A mobile plant operator can let you ride in the machine:

options.B: If it is designed to carry passengers
options.D: If you have a long way to go

questions.explanation: You may only ride in mobile plant if it is purpose-built with a proper seat and restraint for a passenger. Riding on machines not designed to carry people, such as on forks or buckets, risks being thrown off or crushed.

questions.prompt: What must be considered first when planning to carry out work in a confined space?

options.A: Can the work be done from the outside
options.C: Has the job been priced properly
options.D: Have the correct tools been arranged

questions.explanation: Working outside will remove the risks of working in the confined space.

questions.prompt: When working in a confined space, such as a sewer, what danger may occur?

options.D: Not enough time for the job to be done

questions.explanation: Confined spaces like sewers can accumulate toxic, flammable or oxygen-displacing gases that you cannot always see or smell, so air must be tested before entry. Boredom and time pressure are inconveniences, not the life-threatening danger here.

questions.prompt: To determine the safety of the atmosphere in an excavation, which of the following is essential

options.B: Only entering for a short period to enable a quick escape

questions.explanation: Use a suitable detector. Many dangerous gases have no smell, and cannot be seen. Workers can be overcome in seconds in dangerous atmospheres.

questions.prompt: Before entering an excavation to start work, it must first be:
questions.explanation: Excavation work is hazardous. A competent person, knowledgeable about how to reduce risks, notably from collapse of the walls, must inspect the excavation first.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of using a 'permit to work' system?

options.A: To enable tools and equipment to be properly checked before the commencement of work
options.B: To ensure that the client will pay for the work
options.C: To ensure the job is carried out by the quickest method
options.D: To help ensure a safe system of work

questions.explanation: A permit to work is a written system used to control certain types of hazardous work. They allow work to start only when site procedures have been clarified.

questions.prompt: Why may young people be more at risk on site?

options.A: There is no requirement to provide PPE to young people
options.B: There is no specific legislation applying to them
options.C: They are inexperienced and may not recognize danger
options.D: They are usually left to work alone to gain experience

questions.explanation: Health and Safety guidance lists young people as often being 'at particular risk', due to their lack of practical experience.

questions.prompt: You have to enter a manhole in which you know there are toxic gases. You have all the PPE but there does not appear to be a rescue plan in place. What should you do?

options.A: Ask your mate to stand-by at the top of the manhole with a length of rope
options.B: Do not enter the manhole until a rescue plan and rescue equipment are in place
options.C: Just get on and do the job, it will probably be alright
options.D: Plan to carry out the job in short bursts

questions.explanation: A rescue plan must be in place before anyone enters a confined space. This is one of the requirements of the Confined Spaces Regulations 1997.

questions.prompt: You have to enter a manhole in which you believe there could be toxic gases. You have not been provided with any Respiratory Protective Equipment (RPE). What should you do?

options.A: Just get on with the job, and accept the risks
options.B: Look into the manhole to see if you can see any harmful gases
options.C: Sniff the atmosphere in the manhole to see if you can smell harmful gases
options.D: Tell your supervisor that you will need RPE, and if necessary, training in confined space working

questions.explanation: An employer must provide all necessary personal protective equipment and respiratory protective equipment when an employee is required to enter a confined space. This is one of the requirements of the Confined Spaces Regulations 1997.

questions.prompt: While digging a trench, you uncover a length of yellow marker tape at a depth of about 150mm. What does the presence of the marker tape mean?

options.A: The area has a high water-table and precautions must be taken to prevent an in-rush of water
options.B: The excavation has reached a depth where the sides must now be supported
options.C: There is a buried electrical cable and further excavation must be carried out with care
options.D: There is contaminated soil below the level of the marker tape and all excavation must stop

questions.explanation: The coloured tape indicates that there are buried services below the route of the tape.

questions.prompt: A Cable Avoidance Tool (C.A.T.) and a 'Genny' (generator) can be used successfully to locate underground cables by whom:
questions.explanation: Equipment used to locate buried services must only be used by people who have been trained to use it.

questions.prompt: When exposing underground power cables, which method of excavation should you use?

options.A: A 360 degree excavator with rubber tyres

questions.explanation: Hand-held power tools and mechanical excavators should not be used too close to underground services and hand digging should be carried out with care.

questions.prompt: When do special precautions need to be taken when working near overhead electric power lines?

options.A: Only if cranes etc. are being used
options.B: Only if plant has to pass under the lines
options.C: Only if someone could touch a line with their bare hands
options.D: Whenever work areas will be near or beneath the lines

questions.explanation: Actual contact with a power line is not necessary to result in an electric shock as a close approach may allow 'flashover' to occur. HSE publication GS6 gives advice on procedures to avoid such danger.

questions.prompt: When working alone:

options.A: Don't bother anyone if you have a problem, always sort it out yourself
options.B: Make sure someone responsible knows where you are
options.C: Wear headphones, it will make the day go more quickly
options.D: You can do away with protective equipment

questions.explanation: Employees should adhere to safe working arrangements put in place by their employer. When working alone, such arrangements should include informing a responsible person of your location periodically.

questions.prompt: You have to walk across a site several times a day, but have to dodge a lot of site traffic. The first thing you should do is:

options.B: Jump on the back of a vehicle if you can, it's safer than walking
options.C: Tell your supervisor about the danger
options.D: Walk around the edges of the site to keep out of the way

questions.explanation: Pedestrian routes should have been set up to keep people and vehicles apart, so inform your employer if the system is not working. Don't hitch rides on vehicles unless safe seating is provided.

questions.prompt: Why may a confined space be dangerous to work in?

options.A: Air in the space may be unbreathable due to poisonous gas
options.C: Temperature and poor ventilation may affect the worker
options.D: There may not be sufficient working space

questions.explanation: There can be a range of hazards associated with confined spaces, and these can include all of those mentioned

questions.prompt: What action should you take if an electric drill cuts out while you are using it?

options.A: Put it back into the tool box
options.B: Remove it from use and tell your supervisor
options.D: Switch the power off and on

questions.explanation: An electric drill that cuts out may have an internal fault, damaged flex, overheating problem or failing switch. Taking it out of service and reporting it prevents someone else from using unsafe equipment before it is checked.

questions.prompt: If an electric drill gives off blue smoke from the motor, you should:

options.C: Switch it off and report it

questions.explanation: Defective electric hand tools must not be used. Stop what you are doing and inform your supervisor.

questions.prompt: How often should user (visual) checks be carried out on portable electrical equipment?
questions.explanation: All items of portable electrical equipment should be visually checked for safety by the user before being put into use.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred nominal voltage for portable hand lamps for general use on construction sites?
questions.explanation: Site equipment uses 110 V reduced low voltage from a centre-tapped transformer, so a fault only exposes you to about 55 V to earth. This greatly lowers the shock risk compared with 230 V in damp, rough site conditions.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred nominal voltage for portable hand tools on construction sites?
questions.explanation: Portable tools on site run at 110 V from a centre-tapped transformer, giving only around 55 V to earth in a fault. This reduced voltage limits shock severity in the harsh, wet environment of a construction site, far safer than 230 V.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred nominal voltage for local lighting up to 2 kW on construction sites?
questions.explanation: Local site lighting up to 2 kW uses 110 V reduced low voltage, keeping fault voltage to earth around 55 V. This protects workers handling lamps and leads in damp, exposed conditions where 230 V would pose a serious shock hazard.

questions.prompt: What is the recommended maximum voltage for portable hand lamps when working in confined or damp locations?
questions.explanation: Where the environment is damp, or restricting and conductive, the magnitude of any electric shock will be higher than under normal conditions. Hand lamps in such locations should therefore be supplied from a SELV (separated extra-low voltage) system, i.e. having a maximum voltage of 50 volts and which is electrically separated from earth.

questions.prompt: If you only have a mains voltage (230 V) hand drill and you want to use it on a construction site which only has yellow (110 V) socket-outlets, what should you do?

options.A: Cut the plug off and fit a yellow one instead
options.B: Make up an extension cable with a yellow plug on one end and a standard socket on the other end
options.C: Obtain a 110 V drill or a cordless one for the work
options.D: Use a transformer to boost the voltage

questions.explanation: Electrical equipment must not be modified or operated at voltages other than their design voltage.

questions.prompt: What is most commonly used to reduce 230 volts to 110 volts on site?
questions.explanation: A transformer, usually coloured yellow, will transform 230 volts (mains voltage) down to a relatively safe 110 volts.

questions.prompt: When using an extension cable reel, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Do not exceed the reeled or unreeled rating as appropriate
options.B: Leave as much as possible coiled up on the reel

questions.explanation: The rating of a partially unreeled extension cable is much lower than when fully unreeled. Overheating of the cable will occur if the rating is exceeded. Care should also be taken to prevent extension cables becoming a tripping hazard.

questions.prompt: If an extension cable is to be run across a site road, what action should you take?

options.A: Don't do anything to protect the cable
options.B: Lay the cable over wooden boards
options.C: Place a rubber protection ramp over it and put up a sign stating 'Ramp Ahead'

questions.explanation: It is essential that the cable is protected from damage caused by passing traffic. A sign will warn road traffic of the ramp.

questions.prompt: To operate a powered hand tool you must be:
questions.explanation: There are no general age restrictions in legislation relating to the use of work equipment. Any person using work equipment, however, must be competent to do so, which will require initial and refresher training.

questions.prompt: If you are about to use a power tool and discover the guard is missing, you should:

options.A: Make up a temporary guard yourself
options.B: Not use the tool until a proper guard has been fitted
options.C: Use the tool but try to work quickly
options.D: Use the tool but work carefully and slowly

questions.explanation: Visual checks should be carried out before using equipment. Any faults should be reported immediately and rectified before use.

questions.prompt: What do the letters SWL stand for?
questions.explanation: Machinery and accessories for lifting loads should be clearly marked to indicate their safe working loads.

questions.prompt: Who should operate plant and equipment on site?

options.A: An employee holding a full driving license
options.C: Only people over 18 years of age

questions.explanation: Never operate plant or equipment unless you have been trained and are authorised to do so.

questions.prompt: What hazard is created when the head of a cold chisel 'mushrooms'?
questions.explanation: This question is looking for the 'hazard', which is the situation that can cause harm to people.

questions.prompt: Any damaged equipment must be:

options.B: Locked up so no one can use it

questions.explanation: Damaged equipment must be reported to your supervisor so it can be taken out of use, recorded and repaired or replaced. This stops anyone else unknowingly using it, while leaving the decision with the person responsible for site safety.

questions.prompt: The electric drill you are about to use has a faulty on/off switch. What action should you take?

options.A: Find another machine and carry on working
options.B: Stop work and inform your supervisor
options.C: Tape the switch on to keep it running and carry on working

questions.explanation: A faulty on/off switch means you cannot reliably stop the drill, which is dangerous, so you must stop and tell your supervisor. Taping it on or attempting a repair yourself leaves the hazard in place and is not your responsibility.

questions.prompt: The power hand tool you are about to use has burn marks visible on the cable. What should you do?

options.A: Carry on and get the job done
options.B: Obtain another machine and carry on, but don't tell anyone
options.C: Tape over the affected area and continue
options.D: Tell your supervisor about the defect and do not use the tool

questions.explanation: Burn marks on a cable indicate overheating or insulation damage that could cause electric shock or fire, so the tool must be withdrawn and the defect reported. Taping over it or carrying on hides a serious electrical risk.

questions.prompt: Your supervisor asks you to use a powered hand-tool which has a rotating blade. You notice that the guard is missing from the blade. What do you do?

options.A: Contact the manufacturer of the tool
options.B: Inform your supervisor that the tool is unsafe and that the guard must be replaced before it is used
options.C: Try to make an improvised guard yourself
options.D: Use the tool anyway, you haven't had an accident with it before

questions.explanation: A guard protects you from the rotating blade, so a tool with it missing is unsafe and must not be used until the proper guard is fitted. Improvising a guard or relying on past luck does not remove the risk of serious injury.

questions.prompt: Hand and power tools must be:

options.C: Suitable for the task and regularly inspected
options.D: The best that you can buy

questions.explanation: Tools must not create a risk to the user or others. This means they must be suitable and kept in good condition. This requires inspection before use.

questions.prompt: When should visual checks of portable hand-held equipment be made by the user?
questions.explanation: The user needs to be satisfied that the tool has no obvious defect before use.

questions.prompt: What precaution should you take before adjusting an electrical tool?

options.A: Check the lead is not twisted or knotted
options.C: Wear safety footwear with steel toecaps
options.D: Wear the correct personal protective equipment

questions.explanation: Before adjusting an electrical tool you must disconnect it from the supply, so it cannot start unexpectedly and trap or cut you. PPE and checking the lead are sensible, but only isolation removes the danger of accidental energisation.

questions.prompt: An electric drill is to be used. Before use, who should carry out a check on the tool?
questions.explanation: The user must check the tool before use because they are the person about to operate it and are best placed to spot obvious defects there and then. This pre-use inspection catches faults before the tool is put into service.

questions.prompt: What is the best method of securing a ladder?

options.B: Tying it to a suitable point
options.C: Using an effective ladder stability device
options.D: Wedging the ladder (eg against a wall)

questions.explanation: Tying the ladder is the safest option, making sure both stiles are tied.

questions.prompt: Of the following, which is the poorest method of securing a ladder?

options.B: Securing the base of the ladder

questions.explanation: Footing a ladder is the last resort and should be avoided. Other more suitable access equipment should be used where practicable.

questions.prompt: Prior to moving a mobile tower scaffold, the platform height should reduced to a maximum of:
questions.explanation: This figure is quoted in guidance published by the HSE and PASMA. Checks should also be made that there are no obstructions overhead, the ground is firm, level and free from potholes, it is not too windy and there are no people or materials on the tower.

questions.prompt: Ladders should not be painted because:

options.B: The paint may cover a defect or damaged part of the ladder
options.C: The paint may not be suitable on metal parts of the ladder
options.D: The paint will make them slippery to use

questions.explanation: Ladders are left unpainted because paint can hide cracks, splits or other defects that would otherwise be seen during inspection. A concealed fault could fail under load, so the wood or metal is kept visible for safety checks.

questions.prompt: When can you work from a ladder?

options.A: For short periods and then only if it is safe to do so
options.D: When not being used for access

questions.explanation: Ladders are primarily means of access, not workplaces. They can be worked from, but only if the use of other, more suitable, work equipment is not appropriate and the task is of low risk and of short duration.

questions.prompt: When working above public areas, what should be considered?

options.A: Keeping the areas open to the public

questions.explanation: There is a significant risk to the public from falling materials, if this is not considered before and during work.

questions.prompt: A scaffold tower must be erected by:

options.C: The hire company who supply it

questions.explanation: There are a number of organizations that provide training for the safe erection and use of tower scaffolds.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum height of the top guard-rail of a scaffold above the edge from which someone is liable to fall?
questions.explanation: Guard-rails must be high enough to physically stop a person toppling over the edge, so the top rail is set at least 950mm above the working level. The lower options sit too low to arrest a fall and 2 metres would be impractically high.

questions.prompt: A working platform used for construction work, and from which a person could fall 2 metres or more, must not be used unless it has been inspected (and a report is subsequently prepared) by a competent person:
questions.explanation: Under these specific circumstances a report is required to be prepared by the competent person and given to the person for whom the inspection was done (e.g. the site manager). This is in addition to the more general requirement to inspect equipment for work at height: prior to use in that position (or site if it is mobile); following exceptional circumstances (e.g. high winds); and at suitable intervals.

questions.prompt: On a mobile elevating work platform, what should you attach your safety harness to?

options.B: A secure anchorage point inside the platform
options.C: A strong part of the structure you are working on

questions.explanation: The priority is to stay within the platform (which is the safest place), and in any event you cannot be sure of the strength of other fixtures.

questions.prompt: You have been asked to operate a cherry-picker (mobile elevated work platform) when it is very windy. What should your FIRST consideration be?

options.A: Does the wind-speed make it unsafe to use the machine
options.B: Tie all light-weight objects to the hand-rails of the basket
options.C: Wear a safety harness and clip it to the structure that you are working on
options.D: Wear an extra layer of clothing to keep warm

questions.explanation: The priority in safety is eliminating risk at source - in this case by not working in dangerous conditions - rather than trying to stay safe by using protective equipment.

questions.prompt: If you have to work at height and it is not possible to erect a scaffold, or use any other type of working platform or mobile elevating work platform, then you should:

options.A: Wear a harness and lanyard at all times
options.B: Work without fall protection at all times when no one else is about
options.C: Work without fall protection, provided the weather is not too windy
options.D: Work without fall protection, provided you have a mate with you

questions.explanation: The harness will greatly reduce the likelihood of injury if you fall.

questions.prompt: When working on a roof that has fragile, clear-plastic panels, what is the best way of preventing falls through the panels?

options.A: Cover the fragile panels with a strong material and secure the covers to stop them being dislodged
options.B: It shouldn't be necessary to do anything, everyone knows the dangers
options.C: Make sure that everyone is told where the panels are and to avoid treading on them
options.D: Remove the panels carefully to leave an open space.

questions.explanation: Protection from falling through openings and fragile roof lights can be provided by barriers or with covers which can be secured or labelled with a warning.

questions.prompt: When working on fragile roofs:

options.A: As long as you avoid any fragile areas it is safe
options.B: Crawling boards should always be used
options.C: It is safe to walk on the purlins
options.D: Walk straight across the roof to where you need to get to

questions.explanation: Fragile roofs must be made safe to work on, before work commences.

questions.prompt: Half the deaths on construction sites are caused by which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Working at height is the single biggest killer in construction, accounting for around half of all site deaths, which is why fall prevention through guard-rails, edge protection and proper access equipment is such a priority. Plant, electrics and confined spaces cause fewer fatalities by comparison.

questions.prompt: What should you do if your work activity requires you to wear a full body safety harness and one is not available?

options.A: Borrow a harness from a colleague
options.B: Carry on working and hope that everything will be alright
options.C: Make a harness from items found on site
options.D: Stop work immediately and tell your supervisor that you do not have the correct PPE

questions.explanation: Always advise the supervisor if you do not have the correct PPE.

questions.prompt: Under what circumstances do the Work at Height Regulations permit a stepladder to be used on site?

options.C: Only when a risk assessment shows that safer alternatives have been ruled out and the task is of low risk and of short duration
options.D: Provided you can't fall 2 metres or more

questions.explanation: The WAH Regulations have not banned the use of ladders or stepladders, but they should be used sensibly.

questions.prompt: Most deaths on site are caused by:
questions.explanation: Although the other dangers can kill or cause injury, falling from height is the bigger cause of fatalities.

questions.prompt: The type of accident that kills most construction site workers is:
questions.explanation: Although the other dangers can kill or cause injury, falling from height is the biggest cause of fatalities.

questions.prompt: Approximately 70 workers each year die on construction sites, the main cause of this is:
questions.explanation: Falls from height remain the leading cause of construction fatalities because even a short drop onto hard ground or projecting steel can be fatal. This is why edge protection, guard-rails and proper access equipment are central to site safety, far ahead of plant, excavations or fire.

questions.prompt: How many people should be working on a ladder at one time?

options.B: One on each section of an extension ladder
options.C: Three if it is long enough

questions.explanation: Only one person should be working on a ladder, although another person may be footing it, for extra stability.

questions.prompt: Ladders should be set at a slope of approximately:
questions.explanation: A 1-in-4 angle, about 75 degrees, is the stable sweet spot: too shallow and the base slides out, too steep and the ladder tips backwards. Setting it one metre out for every four metres up keeps the climber's weight safely over the stiles.

questions.prompt: Why should aluminium ladders be kept away from wet lime or cement?

options.D: The ladder may become statically charged

questions.explanation: Aluminium can corrode in certain situations, notably if in prolonged contact with lime or cement.

questions.prompt: Before being used, a ladder should be inspected:
questions.explanation: The person about to climb is responsible for checking the ladder is sound, footed properly and free of damage before use, because they are the one at risk and present at the point of use. A pre-use check by the user catches defects a periodic inspection might miss.

questions.prompt: Ladders should be:

options.D: Tied or footed AND at the right angle AND in good condition

questions.explanation: All the measures listed are required to reduce the risk of falls.

questions.prompt: A ladder giving access to a scaffold can generally be safely used, provided that:

options.A: Any broken rungs are clearly marked
options.B: It does not move when you climb up it
options.C: It is tied and extends at least 1 metre above the platform
options.D: The foot of the ladder is firmly wedged

questions.explanation: Access ladders should extend at least 1 metre above the landing point to provide a safe handhold.

questions.prompt: What is the ideal angle for a ladder against a wall and floor?

options.A: Four metres up for every metre out from the wall
options.B: One metre up for every metre out from the wall
options.C: One metre up for every two metres out from the wall
options.D: Two metres up for every metre out from the wall

questions.explanation: The correct angle for a ladder is 75 degrees, which an be judged using the angle indicator marked on the stiles of some ladders or using the 1 in 4 rule.

questions.prompt: The rung of a wooden ladder has started to split, what should you do?

options.B: Do not use it, tell your supervisor
options.C: Jump on it to see if it holds your weight

questions.explanation: A split rung can give way under load and cause a serious fall, so the ladder must be taken out of service and the defect reported to your supervisor to be repaired or scrapped. Taping, cutting or testing it with your weight leaves a dangerous, unreliable ladder in use.

questions.prompt: If you discover a hole or gap in a fire rated wall or floor that has not been fire-stopped, what should you do?

options.A: Cover the hole or gap with insulating tape
options.B: Ignore it unless it is causing a draught
options.C: Report it to your supervisor without delay
options.D: Use decorators' sealant to fill the gap

questions.explanation: Supervisors need to be made aware of any observed inadequacies in fire-stopping - which can undermine fire precautions catastrophically during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

questions.prompt: In addition to preserving fire separation between areas of a building, which other important fire safety function can fire-stopping achieve?
questions.explanation: Fire-stopping also helps maintain the building's structural integrity by protecting load-bearing elements like timber joists and studs that rely on their linings for fire resistance. This buys time before premature collapse, allowing occupants to escape and firefighters to operate safely.

questions.prompt: Intumescent materials used to provide fire-stopping are designed to:
questions.explanation: A limited number of fire-resistant materials may be used to provide fire-stopping. These include intumescent products, which are designed to expand and provide fire-stopping when subjected to heat. Examples include intumescent 'pillows' (used to provide internal sealing of trunking) and intumescent mastic.

questions.prompt: The purpose of fire-stopping in a building is to:

options.B: Delay the passage of fire and smoke through openings in walls and floors

questions.explanation: Fire-stopping is a passive fire protection measure used to seal any openings created in a fire resistance-rated wall or floor assembly, e.g. to allow pipes or wiring systems to pass through. During fire conditions this will impede the spread of fire and smoke.

questions.prompt: What are fire-stops designed to do?

options.B: Delay the passage of fire and smoke through openings in walls and floors
options.D: Protect services (such as wiring systems) against fire damage

questions.explanation: Fire-stops are designed to maintain the fireproofing of a wall or floor assembly. Fire-stopping delays the spread of fire and, generally, the spread of smoke as well.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you disturb fire-stopping around a wiring system penetrating a wall or floor whilst carrying out work?

options.A: Ensure that the fire-stopping is reinstated to the necessary standard as soon as possible
options.B: Fill any holes or gaps with squashed paper
options.D: Nail a piece of wood over any gaps

questions.explanation: It is essential that the integrity of fire compartments is maintained during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Compromising compartmentation, such as failing to adequately fire-stop (seal) openings for services to pass through, can undermine fire precautions catastrophically. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

questions.prompt: What should you do immediately if you get a small cut on a finger whilst at work?

options.A: Ask your employer to report it to the HSE

questions.explanation: It is important to obtain first-aid to prevent further harm (e.g. through infection). It should also be recorded in the accident book (BI 510).

questions.prompt: In an emergency situation at work you should do what?

options.A: Ensure your work mates are all accounted for

questions.explanation: A site emergency plan should have been drawn up and you should be familiar with the emergency procedure.

questions.prompt: What does the sound of a siren on-site normally indicate?
questions.explanation: A site siren is the agreed signal that an emergency has occurred and everyone must stop work and follow the evacuation procedure to the assembly point. It is deliberately general because it could be fire, gas release or another danger, so the response is always to reach a place of safety.

questions.prompt: A red-labelled fire extinguisher should NOT be used:

options.D: Where there is a risk of electrocution

questions.explanation: Red denotes water. Liquids should not be used on electrical fires, since they can conduct electricity.

questions.prompt: A workmate burns their hand on a piece of very hot metal. What should you do first?

options.A: Cover the burn with something dry
options.B: Put their hand in cold water if it is available
options.C: Rub some cream or Vaseline into the burn
options.D: Warn other people about the piece of hot metal

questions.explanation: Cooling a burn under cold running water draws heat out of the tissue and limits how deep the damage spreads. Creams or dry coverings trap heat and can make the injury worse, so cooling the burn always comes first.

questions.prompt: Which of the following items should not be in a first- aid box?
questions.explanation: Drugs must not be kept in a first aid box (Health and Safety guidance note INDG 214).

questions.prompt: How often should a first-aider qualified in First Aid at Work (FAW) or Emergency First Aid at Work (EFAW) receive retraining?
questions.explanation: First Aid at Work (FAW) and Emergency First Aid at Work (EFAW) certificates are valid for three years and first-aiders are required to undertake retraining at the end of this period. However, the HSE also strongly recommends that first-aiders undertake annual (half-day) refresher training.

questions.prompt: If you came across an injury on site, what is the first thing you should do?

options.C: Tell the casualty to visit their doctor
options.D: Try and find out what happened

questions.explanation: Your priority is getting trained medical help to the casualty quickly, so contact a first aider before doing anything else. Investigating the cause or notifying the HSE comes later, and an untrained person should not be left making treatment decisions.

questions.prompt: An employee has a fall and is obviously unconscious. What is the FIRST thing you should do?

options.A: Find out if there were any witnesses
options.B: Put them in the recovery position
options.D: Try to protect them from any further injury

questions.explanation: An unconscious casualty needs trained help urgently, so the immediate action is to send someone for the first aider while you stay to monitor them. Untrained handling like the recovery position could worsen an unseen spinal injury, so leave hands-on care to the trained person.

questions.prompt: A labourer gets an electric shock; looks a bit pale but says they are alright. What should you do?

options.A: Go and check the electrics so it cannot happen again
options.B: See if they want a drink or a cigarette
options.D: Tell them to report it to their supervisor

questions.explanation: An electric shock can disturb the heart rhythm and cause collapse some time later, so even someone who feels fine must be seen by a first aider straight away. Their pale appearance is a warning sign, and a drink or simply reporting it is no substitute for medical assessment.

questions.prompt: Which of the following must an employer consider when making provisions for first aid?

options.B: How much working space will be wasted
options.D: Whether the local ambulance service can be used

questions.explanation: Employers must match first-aid provision to the nature of risks at work.

questions.prompt: In an on-site emergency, which of the following must a first-aider NOT do?

options.B: Give medicines to patients without authorization

questions.explanation: First-aid is concerned with preserving life and limb, and first-aiders are not trained to dispense medical treatments.

questions.prompt: If someone has fallen over and has stopped breathing, what is the first thing you should do?

options.C: Try to give the casualty a drink
options.D: Try to start the casualty breathing

questions.explanation: Do not delay in sending for help; then try to start the casualty breathing.

questions.prompt: If someone has fallen off a ladder and they say their leg is broken, what should you do?

options.B: Help them to the cabin or mess hut
options.C: Move the ladder so no-one trips over it

questions.explanation: A suspected broken leg needs trained assessment, so summon the first-aider and keep the casualty still. Moving them or bandaging their legs could worsen a fracture, and you are not qualified to treat it yourself.

questions.prompt: Your workmate suddenly gets a foreign body in the eye. What should you do?

options.B: Take your workmate to the supervisor
options.C: Use a clean handkerchief to try and remove it
options.D: Wash your hands before touching your mate's face

questions.explanation: Send for the first-aider, who is trained to safely assess and irrigate the eye. Poking with a handkerchief risks scratching the cornea or driving the particle deeper, causing permanent damage.

questions.prompt: A person nearly collapses complaining of stomach pains. What should you do?

options.A: Ask them if they want something to eat
options.B: Go and find them something to drink
options.C: Help them to find somewhere comfortable to sit

questions.explanation: Near-collapse with abdominal pain can signal a serious internal problem, so get the trained first-aider immediately. Giving food or drink could be dangerous if the casualty later needs surgery or worsens.

questions.prompt: A workmate lifting a big box suddenly shouts "oh, my back" and drops the box. What should you do?

options.A: Find them somewhere comfortable to sit and rest
options.B: Help them to lift the box
options.D: Tell them to leave it for someone else to lift

questions.explanation: The priority for any back injury is to obtain first-aid advice, in order to prevent further damage.

questions.prompt: All new fire extinguishers are coloured red or of bright self-coloured metal. How do you know the difference between types?

options.A: A different colour panel or band is on the body of the extinguishers
options.B: During site induction, you will be told where the different types of extinguishers are
options.C: The type of extinguisher is written on a sign next to it
options.D: The weight and shape of the extinguisher

questions.explanation: Different coloured bands show extinguisher types e.g. black for CO2 and blue for dry powder.

questions.prompt: A black-labelled fire extinguisher contains:
questions.explanation: A black label denotes a carbon dioxide (CO2) extinguisher, suited to electrical and flammable-liquid fires because it smothers the flames with gas and leaves no residue to damage equipment.

questions.prompt: What is a blue-labelled fire extinguisher filled with?
questions.explanation: A blue label identifies a dry powder extinguisher, a versatile type that knocks down liquid, gas and electrical fires by interrupting the chemical reaction of combustion.

questions.prompt: Which fire extinguisher should not be used on flammable liquid fires?
questions.explanation: Water must never be used on flammable liquid fires because the burning fuel floats on the water and spreads, while the jet can splash the liquid and rapidly enlarge the fire.

questions.prompt: What colour is a water filled fire extinguisher, or its label?
questions.explanation: Water extinguishers carry an all-red body with a red label. Under the colour-coding scheme red is the base signal colour, and water is the default type that bears no additional coloured panel.

questions.prompt: When discharging carbon dioxide fire extinguishers, the nozzle:
questions.explanation: The expansion of CO2 gas coming out of the nozzle causes rapid cooling.

questions.prompt: For fires involving spilled petrol, which types of fire extinguisher could you use?

options.A: Foam, carbon dioxide or dry powder
options.B: Water, carbon dioxide or dry powder

questions.explanation: Spilled petrol is a flammable liquid (Class B) fire. Foam blankets and seals the surface, while CO2 and dry powder smother the flames. Water is unsafe as it spreads the burning fuel.

questions.prompt: Which types of fire extinguishers should be used on electrical fires?
questions.explanation: CO2 and dry powder are non-conductive, so they will not carry current back to the user. Foam and water conduct electricity and risk electric shock, making them unsafe on live electrical fires.

questions.prompt: What action should you take if you discover a fire?

options.A: Carry on working if it is safe to do so
options.B: Extinguish the fire without raising the alarm
options.C: Leave it because you will get the blame

questions.explanation: Raising the alarm will reduce the risk to others, particularly if the fire spreads.

questions.prompt: If there had been a small fire, who should you report it to?
questions.explanation: The supervisor should be aware, so that further preventative measures can be considered.

questions.prompt: If you discover a fire at work, what should you do first:

options.A: Raise the alarm and warn fellow workers
options.B: Run around looking for an alarm to sound
options.D: Use a fire extinguisher to put it out

questions.explanation: Raising the alarm will reduce the risk to others, particularly if the fire spreads.

questions.prompt: What is a fire assembly point?

options.A: A place where fire extinguishers are kept
options.B: A place where the fire brigade goes to
options.C: The place to go when the fire alarm sounds
options.D: The place where the fire alarm is

questions.explanation: The fire assembly point is the agreed safe place everyone goes to when the alarm sounds, so marshals can take a roll call and confirm no one is left inside the building.

questions.prompt: Where would you go in the event of a fire?

options.A: To the canteen for a cup of tea
options.C: To the fire to see what is going on

questions.explanation: On a fire you evacuate to the designated assembly point, where everyone can be accounted for. Returning to huts or the canteen, or approaching the fire, leaves you in danger and unaccounted for.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you hear the fire alarm?

options.A: Evacuate the premises to a designated place of safety
options.B: Go towards the sound to find out what is going on
options.C: Ignore it because it might be someone playing around

questions.explanation: The alarm means leave at once by the nearest route to the designated place of safety. Investigating or ignoring it wastes vital escape time and puts your life at risk.

questions.prompt: An emergency route(s) must be provided on construction sites to ensure:

options.A: Safe passage to a secure place of safety
options.B: Safe passage to the ground from height
options.C: Safe passage to the open air
options.D: Safe passage to the rest area

questions.explanation: Emergency routes exist to get people away from danger to a defined place of safety, where they are secure and can be accounted for. Simply reaching open air or the ground is not enough if that spot is still within the hazard zone.

questions.prompt: The extended use of powered hand-held tools and equipment may lead to which medical condition?
questions.explanation: Hand-arm vibration can cause a range of conditions (including vibration white finger) collectively known as hand-arm vibration syndrome, as well as diseases such as carpal tunnel syndrome.

questions.prompt: What must your employer do if the daily personal noise exposure is at or exceeds 85 db(A)?

options.A: Issue hearing protection to those exposed and ensure that it is worn
options.B: Provide hearing protection to those employees who ask for it
options.C: Report it to the Health and Safety Executive
options.D: Tell employees to buy their own hearing protection

questions.explanation: This is an interim measure under the Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005 when the daily personal noise exposure is at or exceeds the upper exposure action value of 85 dB(A). Exposure should subsequently be reduced by implementing organizational or technical measures.

questions.prompt: What are the lower and upper action values with regard to daily personal noise exposure, as defined in the Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005?
questions.explanation: Daily personal noise exposure is the average noise level experienced by an individual over an 8 hour period.

questions.prompt: At or above what level of daily personal noise exposure does an employer have to provide hearing protection if it is requested by an employee?
questions.explanation: This is one of the duties of employers under the Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005 when the lower exposure action value of 80 dB(A) is reached or exceeded.

questions.prompt: The effects of damage to your hearing by long-term exposure to high noise levels:

options.B: Can be corrected by an operation
options.C: Can be reversed to near normal, with time
options.D: Will be reduced when you change jobs

questions.explanation: Loud noise destroys the tiny hair cells in the inner ear, and these do not regrow. Once that damage happens it is permanent, which is why hearing protection and reducing exposure matter so much.

questions.prompt: Hearing protection should be worn:
questions.explanation: Employees must wear hearing protectors when exposed at or above the upper exposure action values and within hearing protection zones.

questions.prompt: Wearing suitable hearing protection:

options.A: Brings noise down to an acceptable level

questions.explanation: Hearing protection still allows some noise to reach the ear, but, if it has been correctly chosen, will reduce noise levels to an acceptable level.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is one of the recommended means of protecting your hearing?
questions.explanation: The others are not considered to be suitable types of hearing protection.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not reduce the risks from hand-arm vibration when using a hammer-action tool?

options.A: Making sure one person does all the work with the tool
options.B: Selecting the lowest vibration tool that is suitable and which can do the work efficiently
options.C: Wearing gloves to keep the hands warm
options.D: Working as a team to share the work out

questions.explanation: Where tools require constant or frequent use, rotas will avoid individuals having long exposure to vibration. The use of low-vibration tools and keeping the hands warm in cold conditions will also reduce the risks.

questions.prompt: Which of the following animals can carry Weil's disease?
questions.explanation: Weil's disease is a serious and sometimes fatal infection that can be transmitted to humans by contact with infected rats. Another form of Leptospirosis infection can be transmitted from cattle to humans.

questions.prompt: You are most likely to catch Weil's disease (Leptospirosis) if you:

options.D: Work near wet ground, waterways or sewers

questions.explanation: Anyone who is exposed to rat urine is at risk, particularly sewer workers and farmers. Those in contact with canal or river water are also at risk.

questions.prompt: What should you do if the toilets on your site are continually dirty?

options.A: Ask in a nearby cafe or pub if you can use their toilets
options.B: Find some cleaning materials and clean it up yourself
options.C: Ignore the problem - its normal on a construction site
options.D: Make sure you tell someone who can sort it out

questions.explanation: How often welfare facilities on site require cleaning will depend on the number of people on site and how quickly they get dirty. The person in control of the site should make sure someone is responsible for keeping the facilities clean and tidy.

questions.prompt: Excessive sunlight on bare skin can cause which serious health problem?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet rays in sunlight can cause sunburn and premature ageing of the skin. The most serious effect, however, is an increased chance of developing skin cancer.

questions.prompt: Exposure to asbestos fibres may cause which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Breathing in asbestos fibres can also lead to a number of other diseases, including lung cancer and mesothelioma

questions.prompt: Asbestos is suspected in the workplace, during renovation do you:
questions.explanation: Competent advice must be sought, to prevent exposure to the worker or others, either at the time, or subsequently.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about asbestos is TRUE?

options.A: All forms of asbestos can cause fatal diseases.
options.B: Asbestos is not really a hazard to health
options.C: Only brown and blue asbestos are a hazard to health
options.D: White asbestos is safe to use

questions.explanation: All forms of asbestos can cause fatal diseases. is correct because asbestos exposure can cause fatal disease and must be controlled by trained, authorised people. You should avoid disturbing suspect material and follow the site procedure immediately.

questions.prompt: While working you discover material you think could be asbestos. What should you do?

options.A: Clear any dust and fragments, put them in a bin then carry on working
options.B: Dampen the material to prevent further dust being created, then carry on working
options.D: Stop working immediately and report your suspicions to your supervisor

questions.explanation: It is essential to stop work if asbestos is found or suspected, and await competent advice on what to do next.

questions.prompt: Can you tell by the smell of a product whether it is likely to cause harm?

options.B: Only if you have been trained

questions.explanation: Smell is no guide to safety. Many harmful substances are odourless, while others numb your sense of smell or seem pleasant. You must rely on the safety data sheet and labelling, never your nose, to judge whether something is dangerous.

questions.prompt: How would you recognise a hazardous substance?

options.A: By a symbol on the container
options.C: It will be in a suitable container
options.D: The colour of the label on the container

questions.explanation: A supplier of a packaged hazardous substance must include a label on the packaging incorporating one or more hazard symbols alerting users to the dangers posed by the chemical.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does NOT cause skin problems?
questions.explanation: Asbestos is correct because asbestos exposure can cause fatal disease and must be controlled by trained, authorised people. You should avoid disturbing suspect material and follow the site procedure immediately.

questions.prompt: When an assessment of hazardous substances has been carried out under the COSHH Regulations, the risks and control measures should be explained to:

options.D: the person in charge of the stores

questions.explanation: All those working with the hazardous substances in question need to know about any risks.

questions.prompt: If your hands are very dirty, what should you use to get them clean?
questions.explanation: Soap and water cleans skin without harming it. Solvents like paraffin, thinners and white spirit strip the skin's natural oils, can be absorbed into the body, and cause dermatitis, so they must never be used to wash hands.

questions.prompt: The presence of rats on site creates a risk of catching Weil's disease. What is the EASIEST PRACTICAL MEASURE that you can take to discourage the presence of rats?

options.A: Avoid leaving scraps of food lying about
options.B: Bring a large cat on site
options.C: Contact the local Environmental Health Officer

questions.explanation: The easiest solution is to avoid leaving food around, since this is what attracts vermin.

questions.prompt: Why is personal hygiene so important?

options.A: Because the COSHH regulations require it
options.C: To protect your own and others' health
options.D: To stop you catching something nasty

questions.explanation: Good personal hygiene stops harmful substances on your skin or clothing being swallowed, spread to others, or taken home to family. Washing before eating and after handling materials protects everyone's health, not just your comfort.

questions.prompt: If you have been handling lead, how is it most likely to get into your blood stream?

options.A: By not reporting the matter to the HSE
options.B: By not using the correct safety footwear
options.C: By not washing your hands before eating

questions.explanation: The route into the body is ingestion, normally from lead contamination on the hands.

questions.prompt: The number of toilets provided on site depends on:

options.A: The duration of the work on site
options.B: The number of personnel on site
options.C: The ratio of male and female workers on site
options.D: The type of work being completed

questions.explanation: Guidance on the provision of welfare facilities is given in HSE publication 'Health and Safety in Construction'.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not required to be provided under the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations?
questions.explanation: Guidance on the provision of welfare facilities as required by CDM is given in HSE publication 'Health and Safety in Construction'.

questions.prompt: When should you wear safety footwear on site?

options.A: Only if the site conditions are wet
options.D: When there is a risk of a foot injury

questions.explanation: Suitable safety footwear should be worn if there is a risk of injury from objects falling onto the foot or sharp objects, such as nails, penetrating the sole.

questions.prompt: With regard to the use of personal protective equipment (PPE), which one of the following statements is true?

options.A: If you do not use the personal protective equipment (PPE) provided you will probably not come to any harm
options.B: Personal protective equipment (PPE) need only be provided if it is not too expensive
options.C: Personal protective equipment (PPE) need only be used if it is available
options.D: Personal protective equipment (PPE) protects only the user from the dangers present

questions.explanation: PPE is there to protect the individual. Wearing PPE does not protect other people nearby.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is TRUE when an employer issues personal protective equipment (PPE)?

options.A: The employer can charge you for the full cost of it
options.B: The employer can charge you for up to half the cost of it
options.C: The employer can only charge you for it if you lose or damage it
options.D: The employer cannot charge you for it

questions.explanation: Employers cannot charge for PPE such as hard hats, gloves, required by law (and the bulk of PPE is required by law).

questions.prompt: Which one of the following must apply to any hard hat provided?

options.B: It is less than 1 year old
options.C: It is less than 2 years old
options.D: It is less than 5 years old

questions.explanation: PPE must meet a recognised safety standard, shown by the CE (now UKCA) mark, proving it was tested and made to protect properly. Age alone says nothing about whether a hard hat is fit for use.

questions.prompt: When using personal protective equipment (PPE) legally you must do which of the following?

options.A: Clean it properly once a week
options.B: Not interfere with it or misuse it
options.C: Replace it at your own expense if it is damaged
options.D: Return it to the manufacturer when damaged

questions.explanation: Interfering with or misusing items provided in the interests of health, safety or welfare is an offence under the HSW Act 1974 (section 8)

questions.prompt: If it is necessary for an employee to use personal protective equipment, who has a duty to provide it?
questions.explanation: This is a requirement of the PPE at Work Regulations 1992 (Regulation 4).

questions.prompt: When should a safety helmet be worn on site?

options.A: At all times unless there is no foreseeable risk of injury to the head other than by falling.
options.C: When walking to and from a place of work
options.D: When you are out in the open air

questions.explanation: The circumstances when there is no foreseeable risk of head injury from falling or swinging objects or striking the head against something will be very limited in most construction work.

questions.prompt: A colleague has drilled holes in the top of his safety helmet because the weather is hot. Is this:

options.B: Acceptable if the holes are small

questions.explanation: Interfering with or misusing items provided in the interests of health, safety or welfare is an offence under the HSW Act 1974 (section 8).

questions.prompt: Who has a duty to provide PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) for use by an employee?
questions.explanation: This is a requirement of the PPE at Work Regulations 1992(Regulation 4).

questions.prompt: When would it be appropriate to wear a bump-cap instead of a safety helmet?

options.B: Whenever a safety helmet feels uncomfortable
options.C: When there is no foreseeable risk of injury from falling or swinging objects

questions.explanation: Industrial scalp protectors (bump caps) can protect against striking fixed obstacles, scalping or entanglements. They do not provide suitable protection against falling or swinging objects.

questions.prompt: How can you protect your eyesight while working on site?

options.A: By not looking directly at what you are doing
options.D: By wearing the correct type of eye protection

questions.explanation: The eyes can only be reliably protected by a physical barrier matched to the hazard, such as goggles or a face shield against dust, sparks or chemicals. Squinting or looking away cannot stop flying particles reaching the eye.

questions.prompt: When is head protection required to be worn on a construction site to comply with the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations?

options.A: At all times except by those who are self employed
options.B: At all times unless there is no foreseeable risk of injury to the head other than by falling.
options.C: At all times unless you are working on scaffold
options.D: Only when you feel like it

questions.explanation: If there is no risk of injury to the head, then hard hats are not required by law. However, on construction sites, despite controls being in place, there will almost always be situations where a risk of head injury remains and require head protection to be worn. Site rules will also require the wearing of head protection other than in any designated safe areas.

questions.prompt: Why should a high visibility vest be worn when working on roads?

options.A: Because it will keep you warm
options.B: Because you were told to do so
options.C: So road users and plant operators can see you
options.D: So that your mates can see you

questions.explanation: So road users and plant operators can see you is correct because site transport and plant risks are controlled by separation, competence, visibility, and following the planned system of work. The chosen option reduces the chance of being struck or crushed.

questions.prompt: When considering what measures to take to protect people's health and safety, PPE should always be regarded as:

options.A: The best way to tackle the job

questions.explanation: Engineering controls and safe systems of work should always be considered first.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following should you do if your personal protective equipment (PPE) is damaged?

options.C: Reduce the amount of time you use it
options.D: Report to your Supervisor without delay
