questions.explanation: Employees are required to report any defective PPE to their employer (PPE at Work Regulations 1992, Regulation 7)

questions.prompt: If personal protective equipment (PPE) is defective, what should you do?

options.A: Complain to the Health and Safety Inspector
options.B: Get your work mate to mend it if possible
options.C: Repair if possible and continue to use it

questions.explanation: Employees are required to report any defective PPE to their employer (PPE at Work Regulations 1992, Regulation 7)

questions.prompt: In normal use, what item of PPE is NOT essential for the operator of a cartridge-operated tool, such as a nail gun?
questions.explanation: Wellingtons do not offer protection against the specific risks associated with the use of a cartridge-operated tool, although safety footwear must always be worn when there is a risk of a foot injury.

questions.prompt: Can you opt out of wearing personal protective equipment (PPE)?

options.B: Yes, by informing the site supervisor
options.C: Yes, by writing officially to your employer

questions.explanation: You cannot legally "opt out" of being protected from significant risks at work. This includes wearing the necessary PPE.

questions.prompt: What is the most important item of personal protective equipment (PPE) when working on or near a highway?
questions.explanation: Near traffic the biggest risk is being struck by a vehicle, so being seen comes first. A high-visibility vest makes you conspicuous to drivers, giving them time to react, which other PPE cannot do.

questions.prompt: If you are drilling into concrete with a masonry drill, in which one of the following circumstances will you need to wear eye protection?

options.B: Not if drilling into the floor
options.C: Only if the drill is bigger than 10mm

questions.explanation: Suitable eye protection must always be worn when working with power-driven tools where chippings are likely to fly or abrasive materials could be propelled.

questions.prompt: When must you wear all personal protective equipment (PPE) provided by your employer?
questions.explanation: Under the PPE at Work Regulations 1992, employees must wear PPE as instructed.

questions.prompt: When MUST an employer provide their employees with personal protective equipment (PPE)?

options.B: If the client or main contractor specifies it in the contract
options.D: When they may be exposed to a risk to their health & safety which cannot be controlled another way

questions.explanation: PPE is the last resort in the hierarchy of control. An employer must provide it whenever a risk to health and safety remains that cannot be removed or controlled by other means, regardless of contracts or fixed timescales.

questions.prompt: What type of eye protection would you wear when using a cartridge-operated tool, such as a nail gun?
questions.explanation: When using a cartridge-operated tool, such as a nail gun, shatter proof goggles should be worn.

questions.prompt: Which of the following must your safety helmet comply with to meet with the requirements of the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations?

options.A: It can be adjusted to suit your head size
options.B: It has a label with your name on it
options.C: It is a good visible colour
options.D: It is less than 1 year old

questions.explanation: An assessment of the suitability of head protection would include consideration of whether it can be adjusted to suit the individual who is to wear it, that it is compatible with the work to be done and that it is comfortable to wear.

questions.prompt: In which of the following ways should you wear your safety helmet?

options.A: Square on your head, properly adjusted
options.B: With the helmet back to front
options.C: With the peak raised to deflect falling material
options.D: With the peak raised to give good vision

questions.explanation: Any item of personal protective equipment must be used in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions, which will include how to correctly fit and wear it and what its limitations are.

questions.prompt: When an employee has been issued with eye protection, what are their duties under the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations?

options.A: Not to loan the equipment to other operatives
options.B: To ensure that they are the right type of protector
options.C: To pay for replacement of lost eye protection
options.D: To use the protection in accordance with training and instruction

questions.explanation: Regulation 10(2) requires that every employee shall use any PPE in accordance with the training and instruction received.

questions.prompt: When working in dusty conditions, what of the following would give the LEAST level of protection?
questions.explanation: Protection factors are given in HSE publication HSG53 'Respiratory protective equipment at work - A practical guide'

questions.prompt: In hot weather which one of the following is correct with regard to safety helmets?

options.A: You can drill holes in your safety hat for ventilation
options.B: You can take off your helmet while working inside the building
options.C: You do not need to wear your helmet
options.D: You must continue to wear your helmet

questions.explanation: On construction sites, despite controls being put in place, there will always be situations where a risk of head injury remains. Taking off your helmet would put you at a much greater risk of a head injury and any unauthorised modification would be in breach of legal requirements and could render the helmet next to useless.

questions.prompt: If there is a fatal accident on site, when must the Health and Safety Executive be informed?
questions.explanation: A fatality is the most serious reportable event under RIDDOR, so the HSE must be told straight away by the quickest means, without delay. Written follow-up reports come later, but immediate notification cannot wait days.

questions.prompt: Under which of the following circumstances should an accident be recorded in the site's accident book?

options.A: Only when a person is injured and will be off work for more than seven days
options.B: When an accident causes damage to plant or equipment
options.C: When an accident causes injury to an employee while at work
options.D: When the injury is serious enough for first aid to be needed.

questions.explanation: The accident book records any injury an employee suffers at work, however minor. This creates a legal record for the employee's benefit and helps spot trends; damage to plant or the need for first aid are not the trigger for an entry.

questions.prompt: Which of the following have to be entered into the accident book?

options.D: Only accidents causing time off work

questions.explanation: Every accident causing an injury must be entered, not just serious ones or those leading to time off. A small injury can later prove significant, and a full record protects the worker and helps identify recurring hazards.

questions.prompt: Under which of the following circumstances must injury accidents be recorded in the accident book?

options.B: Only if you break a bone
options.C: Only if you have time off work
options.D: Only if you need to go to hospital

questions.explanation: All injury accidents must be logged whenever they happen, however minor they seem. A small injury can worsen later, and a contemporaneous record protects both you and the employer and helps spot recurring hazards.

questions.prompt: An entry must be made in the accident book when:

options.A: an accident causes personal injury to an employee
options.C: the person has been off sick for over seven days
options.D: the severity of the accident may result in a compensation claim

questions.explanation: Any accident causing personal injury to an employee must be entered, regardless of severity or whether a claim or sick leave follows. Recording every injury creates evidence and lets the employer investigate and prevent a repeat.

questions.prompt: Which of the following MUST be recorded in an accident book after you have had an accident?
questions.explanation: The information to be entered in an accident book (BI510) includes when and where the accident happened, the name, address and occupation of the person who had the accident and details of how the accident happened and the injuries suffered.

questions.prompt: Which of the following can you learn from an accident?

options.A: A combination of human error and mechanical failure always causes injury
options.B: How human error is always a cause
options.C: Ideas on how you would prevent it happening again
options.D: That mechanical failures are most dangerous

questions.explanation: An accident investigation should not only assess the cause, but also how similar accidents can be prevented in the future.

questions.prompt: Could making an entry in the accident book help you if you later make a claim for compensation?

options.B: Only if it is a serious injury
options.C: Only in the event of a fatality

questions.explanation: Yes, because the entry is a dated, factual record made at the time, providing evidence that the accident happened at work. Without it, proving how and when an injury occurred for a later claim becomes far harder.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to report 'near miss' accidents to your employer?

options.B: So lessons can be learned, preventing an accident next time
options.C: So that someone can be disciplined
options.D: To make the figures look good

questions.explanation: The HSE advises that 'near misses' should be investigated to prevent their recurrence.

questions.prompt: Who should you report serious accidents to?
questions.explanation: Report serious accidents to your employer or supervisor, who can secure the scene, prevent a recurrence, and discharge the legal duty to notify the enforcing authority. Emergency services treat casualties but are not who you formally report to.

questions.prompt: What is the aim of carrying out an accident investigation?

options.A: To determine the cause(s) and prevent similar accidents
options.B: To establish the cost of any damage incurred
options.C: To establish what injuries were sustained
options.D: To find out who is at fault

questions.explanation: An accident investigation should not only assess the cause, but also how similar accidents can be prevented in the future.

questions.prompt: You have witnessed a serious accident on your site and are interviewed by an HSE inspector. Should you:

options.A: Ask your supervisor what you should say to the inspector
options.B: Co-operate fully with the inspector and tell him exactly what you saw
options.D: Tell the inspector what your mates say you should tell him

questions.explanation: This is good practice, but it can also be an offence to withhold important information from an inspector.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following accounts for most accidents each year on construction sites?
questions.explanation: HSE statistics show clearly that there are more slips, trips and falls than any other type of accident on site.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT classified as a specified injury to a worker under RIDDOR?
questions.explanation: Amputation of an arm, hand, finger, thumb, leg, foot or toe are classified as specified injuries, as are bone fractures other than to fingers, thumbs or toes.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following should you do if you witness a serious accident on site?

options.A: Discuss what to do with your workmates
options.C: Say nothing in case you get in trouble
options.D: Tell your supervisor what you saw happening

questions.explanation: Tell your supervisor exactly what you saw, as your account helps establish the cause and allows action to stop it happening again. Staying quiet or covering up leaves the hazard in place and breaches your safety duties.

questions.prompt: A workmate tells you that he witnessed an accident the previous day and the victim was taken to hospital. He asks you for advice on what he should do. Do you tell him to:

options.A: Say nothing to anyone in case he gets someone in trouble
options.B: Speak to the site nurse about what he saw
options.C: Telephone the hospital to find out how the injured person is
options.D: Tell his supervisor that he saw what happened

questions.explanation: He should report what he witnessed to his supervisor, as his account aids the investigation and helps prevent a repeat. Phoning the hospital or staying silent does nothing to address the cause of the accident.

questions.prompt: If a person at work suffers an injury (other than a specified injury) due to an accident at work, it is reportable under RIDDOR if they are incapacitated for work for:
questions.explanation: An over-seven-day injury is one which is not a specified injury but results in the injured person being away from work or unable to do the full range of their normal duties for more than seven days (including any days they wouldn't normally be expected to work such as weekends, rest days or holidays) not counting the day of the injury itself.

questions.prompt: What must an employer do with their accident records following completion of a construction project?

options.A: They are destroyed on site with other non-essential documents
options.B: They are kept safe by the employer
options.C: They are sent to the Health and Safety Executive
options.D: They are sent to the employer's insurance company

questions.explanation: Accident records must be kept by an employer for at least three years.

questions.prompt: At work who would you report a dangerous occurrence to?
questions.explanation: Under RIDDOR, an employer has a legal duty to report certain work-related accidents, but to do this they will need to know that an accident has occurred.

questions.prompt: Following a reportable dangerous occurrence when must the enforcing authority be informed?
questions.explanation: A reportable dangerous occurrence must be notified to the enforcing authority without delay, as the immediate hazard could harm others again at any moment. Prompt notification lets investigation and control measures begin straight away.

questions.prompt: Accidents causing any injury should always be recorded in:
questions.explanation: Injury accidents go into your employer's accident recording system, which is the legally recognised record. Personal diaries or another contractor's day book carry no formal status and would not reliably support an investigation or claim.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is classified as a reportable occupational disease under RIDDOR?
questions.explanation: Certain occupational diseases likely to have been caused or made worse by work are reportable under RIDDOR. This would include occupational asthma where the person's work includes significant or regular exposure to a known respiratory sensitizer.

questions.prompt: When a person is injured at work, who should enter the details in the accident book?

options.A: The injured person or anyone acting for them

questions.explanation: This is the procedure for recording accidents internally in the accident book(BI 510).

questions.prompt: If you are involved in a minor accident at work, whose duty is it to report it to site management?

options.C: The police, fire or ambulance who attend
options.D: The site foreman should report it

questions.explanation: Reporting your own minor accident is your responsibility, since you are the person who knows it happened. Relying on a witness or foreman to notice and report risks the incident going unrecorded and the hazard remaining.

questions.prompt: You have suffered an accident at work which has made you incapable of your normal work for over 7 days. Which of the following actions MUST be taken by your employer?

options.A: A deduction is made from your wages for days lost
options.B: The emergency services are asked to attend the site
options.D: The relevant enforcing authority is informed

questions.explanation: An over-seven-day injury is one which is not a specified injury but results in the injured person being away from work or unable to do the full range of their normal duties for more than seven days (including any days they wouldn't normally be expected to work such as weekends, rest days or holidays) not counting the day of the injury itself.

questions.prompt: The collapse of scaffolding is only notifiable to the enforcing authority as a reportable dangerous occurrence when the scaffolding is which one of the following?
questions.explanation: A scaffolding collapse becomes a reportable dangerous occurrence once the structure is over 5 metres high, the height at which a collapse carries serious risk of major injury. Below that threshold it is not separately notifiable as a dangerous occurrence.

questions.prompt: What should you ensure if you suffer an injury through a manual handling operation?

options.B: You get help and carry on working
options.C: You get paid for the job

questions.explanation: All injuries must be recorded in the Company accident book (BI 510)

questions.prompt: Why should a serious accident be reported to the enforcing authority?

options.A: It helps the site find out what caused it
options.C: So that the company will be held responsible
options.D: So that the site manager can see who is to blame

questions.explanation: Serious accidents (specified injuries or those resulting in an absence of over 7 days) must be reported to the enforcing authority under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR).

questions.prompt: What immediate action should you take if you suffer an injury through carrying a load?

options.A: Advise your doctor of your injury
options.B: Carry on working as best you can

questions.explanation: All injuries must be recorded in the Company accident book (BI 510).

questions.prompt: Under RIDDOR, which one of the following must be reported to the enforcing authority?

options.A: Accidents where the injured person wishes to make a claim
options.B: All 'near misses' even if no one is hurt
options.D: Fracture other than to fingers, thumbs or toes

questions.explanation: This is one of a number of reportable 'specified injuries' and must be reported to the enforcing authority under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR).

questions.prompt: Which one of the following has the power to examine an accident record?
questions.explanation: An HSE inspector has statutory powers to examine accident records as part of enforcing health and safety law. A doctor, workmate or insurer has no such legal right of access to the records.

questions.prompt: Which of the following should be recorded in the accident book following an accident?

options.A: The date and time the accident occurred

questions.explanation: The information to be entered in an accident book (BI510) includes when and where the accident happened, the name, address and occupation of the person who had the accident and details of how the accident happened and the injuries suffered. The weather conditions would only be included if they contributed to the accident

questions.prompt: What should you do first before lifting or moving a load?
questions.explanation: You or your employer must assess the risk of injury before lifting.

questions.prompt: Before picking up a load, you should:

options.A: Ask a work mate to help you

questions.explanation: You or your employer must assess the risk of injury before lifting.

questions.prompt: When picking up an object, you should:
questions.explanation: Generally, the legs should do most of the work when lifting a load.

questions.prompt: When judging "individual capability" for manual handling, you should assume:
questions.explanation: Assessing ability for manual handling must be done on an individual basis.

questions.prompt: When an article has to be moved for a long distance, you should:

options.C: Get someone else to do it for you

questions.explanation: Using a barrow or trolley lets the wheels carry the weight over the distance, sparing your back and reducing the risk of strain. Carrying or dragging a load a long way greatly increases manual-handling injury.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct way to lift a load?

options.A: Keep feet apart and bend back
options.B: Keep feet together and bend back
options.C: Squat near load, bend back and use leg muscles
options.D: Squat near to the load, keeping the back as straight as possible and using leg muscles

questions.explanation: Handling techniques which allow the use of relatively strong leg muscles rather than those of the back are preferable.

questions.prompt: Which would you consider to be generally correct when lifting a load?

options.A: Keep the load away from the body
options.B: Larger loads should be split into smaller loads if possible
options.C: The feet should be together and the load lifted at arm's length
options.D: When lifting you should bend your back

questions.explanation: Splitting a large load into smaller parts reduces the weight handled in one go, keeping it within safe limits and cutting the strain on the spine. The wrong options describe poor technique: hold loads close, keep feet apart and your back straight.

questions.prompt: If a load has an uneven centre of gravity, how should you lift it?

options.A: Keep the heaviest side of the load away from you
options.B: Keep the heaviest side of the load on the strongest arm
options.C: Keep the heaviest side of the load on the weakest arm
options.D: Keep the heaviest side of the load towards you

questions.explanation: There is less risk of injury if a weight's centre of gravity is near the torso.

questions.prompt: What would you NOT consider in making a judgement of the risks from a load?
questions.explanation: A, C and D can all affect the difficulty of lifting an object.

questions.prompt: When moving a load fitted with wheels which of the following is generally true?

options.A: It is safer to pick it up and carry it
options.C: Pushing and pulling are equally risky

questions.explanation: The operator should try to push rather than pull when moving a load, provided they can see over it and control steering and stopping.

questions.prompt: A manual handling operation is defined as which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Manual handling means moving a load by human effort alone, such as lifting, lowering, pushing, pulling or carrying. Once a machine like a forklift or crane does the work it is mechanical handling, not manual.

questions.prompt: What is the MAXIMUM weight that an individual may lift?

options.A: 15kg provided that it is a compact load
options.B: 35kg provided that it has no sharp edges
options.C: The weight they can lift comfortably

questions.explanation: There are no strict weight limits - the priority is to avoid injury.

questions.prompt: What is the most common type of injury resulting from lifting loads from the floor?
questions.explanation: Lifting from floor level forces you to bend and take the strain through the lower spine, so the back is the body part most often injured. This is why you bend the knees and keep the load close rather than stooping.

questions.prompt: Where a load has to be lifted manually, what is the employer required to do by law?

options.A: Assess the risk of the task
options.B: Assess the time the job will take
options.C: Calculate the cost of the exercise
options.D: Determine the number of people required

questions.explanation: This is a specific requirement of the Manual Handling Operations regulations 1992.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is advisable when lifting a load manually?

options.A: Bend the knees, keep the back as straight as possible, use power of legs
options.B: Bend the knees, keep the back straight, use power of back
options.C: Keep legs and back straight, use power of legs
options.D: Keep legs straight, bend back, use power of legs

questions.explanation: Stooping can increase the stress on the lower back. However, stooping slightly may be preferable to adopting a squatting posture, which can place excessive loads on knees and hips.

questions.prompt: In manual handling, which of the following general statements is true?

options.A: Anyone can carry any load as long as they are strong enough
options.B: Large loads should be broken down into smaller loads where possible
options.C: Loads should be held at arm's length while carrying
options.D: You should keep your back bent when lifting

questions.explanation: Breaking a large load into smaller parts keeps each lift within safe limits and reduces strain on the spine. The other statements are unsafe: not everyone can handle every load, hold loads close not at arm's length, and keep the back straight.

questions.prompt: What is the recommended limit for a compact load that can be safely carried by a fit, male worker?
questions.explanation: This figure is in HSE guidance, and relates to lifting and lowering at elbow height.

questions.prompt: Where there has been a major change in a manual handling operation, what should the employer do?

options.C: Review the number of people involved

questions.explanation: This is a specific requirement of the Manual Handling Operations regulations 1992.

questions.prompt: What should be the first consideration when you are about to lift a load on your own?

options.A: Assess whether it is safe to lift it on your own
options.B: Ensure you lift with a bent back

questions.explanation: Employees should assess whether there is a risk of injury before lifting. If they are not sure they should seek advice from their supervisor.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would NOT make a load easier to handle manually

options.B: Providing suitable handles or hand grips
options.D: Securing the load so that it does not shift unexpectedly

questions.explanation: A bright colour only changes appearance, not how heavy or awkward the load is to lift. Handles, lighter weight and a secured, stable load all genuinely reduce the physical effort and risk of injury.

questions.prompt: If there is a risk of injury from moving loads what should you think about?

options.D: Getting someone to assist you over the distance

questions.explanation: If a lift looks likely to cause injury you should raise it with your supervisor so the task can be reassessed and safer methods or equipment arranged. Carrying on regardless or dragging the load just risks harm.

questions.prompt: As an approximate guide the manual handling capacity of a two person team is:

options.A: The capacity of the strongest individual
options.B: The capacity of the weakest individual
options.C: The sum of their individual capacities
options.D: Two thirds the sum of their individual capacities

questions.explanation: This is contained in HSE guidance on the Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992.

questions.prompt: What does 'Kinetic lifting' mean?

options.A: Getting a friend to help you with the load
options.B: Lifting in the most safe and effective way
options.C: Using a crane or some other mechanical means
options.D: Using a forklift truck or pallet truck

questions.explanation: Kinetic lifting is the recognised technique for lifting by hand in the safest, most efficient way: feet apart, knees bent, back straight and load held close so the legs do the work. It does not involve machinery or a helper.

questions.prompt: If there is a risk of injury from lifting loads what should you think about first?

options.B: What the weight of the load is
options.C: Where to hold the load when lifting
options.D: Whether the load needs to be lifted at all

questions.explanation: If possible, it is best to avoid the risks from lifting altogether. This is the preferred requirement laid down in the Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992.

questions.prompt: Before performing manual lifting what is the first thing you should do?

options.C: Kick it to see if it is stable

questions.explanation: If you assess the whole task first, you will have a clear idea of possible hazards and how to overcome them, before lifting

questions.prompt: Which is the part of your body MOST LIKELY to be injured during a manual handling activity which involves moving a heavy load?
questions.explanation: Moving a heavy load puts the greatest stress on the lower spine, especially if you bend or twist, so the back is the most likely part to be injured. Good technique protects the back by letting the legs take the strain.

questions.prompt: What should you do if your supervisor asks you to move something that you find is too heavy to lift?

options.A: Ask your mates to assist in the lift
options.B: Get a forklift truck or lifting tackle
options.C: Give it a try using correct lifting methods
options.D: Inform your supervisor that it is too heavy

questions.explanation: The HSE advises employees to inform the employer if they identify hazardous handling activities

questions.prompt: Why would your supervisor ask you to read the method statement and risk assessment before you start your next job?

options.A: As someone has taken the time and trouble to write them, you might as well read them
options.B: He thinks you have got nothing better to do
options.C: He wouldn't, he thinks they are a waste of time
options.D: They contain information on how to carry out the job in a safe manner

questions.explanation: The supervisor must, by law, keep workers advised of significant risks, and control measures.

questions.prompt: What do the blue and white health and safety signs tell you?

options.D: Where the nearest fire exit is

questions.explanation: Blue and white signs are mandatory signs telling you something you must do, such as wearing PPE. Prohibition signs (must not) are red, warnings are yellow, and fire exits are green.

questions.prompt: What colours are fire exit signs?
questions.explanation: The colours are prescribed in the Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations.

questions.prompt: What is the main colour on a safety sign stating that you must NOT do something?
questions.explanation: Prohibitory signs are round and feature a black pictogram on a white background with red edging and diagonal line.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations require the colour coding of signs. What colours are used on a sign indicating a warning, for example "Fork-lift trucks operating"?
questions.explanation: Warning signs use a yellow background with black symbols and border, a high-contrast combination chosen to catch the eye and alert you to a hazard such as moving vehicles. Blue means mandatory, red prohibition, and green safe condition.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations require the colour coding of safety signs. What colours are used on a sign indicating a prohibited activity, for example "No access for pedestrians"?
questions.explanation: Prohibitory signs are round and feature a black pictogram on a white background with red edging and diagonal line.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations require the colour coding of safety signs. What colours are used on a sign indicating a mandatory activity, for example "Safety helmets must be worn"?
questions.explanation: Mandatory signs, which instruct you to carry out an action like wearing a safety helmet, use a blue circle with a white symbol. Yellow and black warns of hazards, while red is used for prohibition and fire signs.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations require the colour coding of safety signs. What colours are used on a sign indicating a safe condition, for example "First Aid kit"?
questions.explanation: Emergency escape and first-aid signs are rectangular or square and feature a white pictogram on a green background.

questions.prompt: Why should regular inspections of the workplace take place?

options.A: To check that all employees are present
options.B: To check that everyone is doing their job
options.C: To check whether the working environment is safe
options.D: To prepare for a visit from an HSE Inspector

questions.explanation: The Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations require that routine inspections of workplaces are carried out to ensure that preventative and protective measures are in place and effective.

questions.prompt: How can you help to prevent accidents?

options.B: Know how to get help quickly
options.C: Know where the first-aid kit is kept

questions.explanation: Action to improve safety can only be taken if the risk is known about. Employees have a duty of care to other employees.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 and any regulations made under the Act are:

options.C: Not compulsory, but should be complied with if convenient
options.D: Practical advice for the employer to follow

questions.explanation: The requirements of health and safety law are mandatory and failure to follow them can lead to prosecution.

questions.prompt: Under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, which of the following have a duty to work safely?
questions.explanation: Employers, employees and the self-employed all have duties to work safely under the Act.

questions.prompt: What is the MAXIMUM penalty that a Higher Court, can currently impose for a breach of the Health and Safety at Work Act?

options.A: Unlimited fine and two years imprisonment

questions.explanation: A Lower Court can impose a fine of up to £20,000 and/or up to six months imprisonment for certain offences. The potential fine in a Higher Court, however, is unlimited and the term of imprisonment can be up to 2 years.

questions.prompt: What do the letters ACoP stand for?
questions.explanation: An ACOP is a code of practice approved by the Health and Safety Executive (or the Health and Safety Commission prior to April 2008).

questions.prompt: Where should you look for Official advice on health and safety matters?

options.A: A professionally approved guide book on regulations
options.B: A set of health and safety guidelines provided by suppliers
options.C: Guidance issued by the Health and Safety Executive
options.D: The health and safety rules as laid down by the employer

questions.explanation: The HSE is the UK enforcing body and its guidance can be regarded as 'official'

questions.prompt: Regulations that govern health and safety on construction sites:

options.D: Do not apply during 'out of hours' working

questions.explanation: The requirements of health and safety law are mandatory, and failure to follow them can lead to prosecutions.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: All employees must take reasonable care, not only to protect themselves but also their colleagues
options.B: Employees have no responsibility for Health and Safety on site
options.C: Only the client is responsible for safety on site
options.D: The duty for health and safety falls only on the employer

questions.explanation: This is a legal requirement under Section 7 of the Health & Safety at Work Act.

questions.prompt: Who of the following would you expect to be responsible for managing health and safety on site?
questions.explanation: The responsibility for management of health and safety at work rests with the employer.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is correct for risk assessment?

options.A: It is a good idea but not essential
options.B: It can be completed after the work is finished

questions.explanation: There is a legal requirement for all work to be suitably risk assessed.

questions.prompt: In the context of a risk assessment, what do you understand by the term risk?

options.B: Any work activity that can be described as dangerous
options.C: Something with the potential to cause injury
options.D: The likelihood that harm from a particular hazard will occur

questions.explanation: Hazard and risk are not the same. Risk reflects the chance of being harmed by a hazard

questions.prompt: Who would you expect to carry out a risk assessment on your working site?
questions.explanation: Risk assessments must be carried out by a competent person, someone with the right training, knowledge and experience to identify hazards and judge sensible controls. An HSE inspector enforces the law rather than doing the site's own assessments.

questions.prompt: What is a HAZARD?

options.B: Something with the potential to cause harm
options.C: The likelihood of something going wrong
options.D: Where an accident is likely to happen

questions.explanation: Examples of hazards include: a drum of acid, breeze blocks on an elevated plank; cables running across a floor.

questions.prompt: What must be done before any work begins?
questions.explanation: This is a legal requirement of the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations.

questions.prompt: Complete the following sentence: A risk assessment

options.A: Is a means of analysing what might go wrong
options.B: Is a piece of paper required by law

questions.explanation: Risk assessment involves a careful review of what can cause harm and the practical measures to be taken to reduce the risk of harm.

questions.prompt: What happens if a Prohibition Notice is issued by an Inspector of the local authority or the HSE?

options.A: The work can continue if adequate safety precautions are put in place
options.B: The work can continue, provided a risk assessment is carried out
options.C: The work in hand can be completed, but no new work started
options.D: The work that is subject to the notice must cease

questions.explanation: The work activity covered by a prohibition notice must cease, until the identified danger is removed.

questions.prompt: A Health and Safety Executive Inspector can?

options.A: Only visit if accompanied by the principal contractor
options.B: Only visit if they have made an appointment
options.C: Only visit to interview the site manager

questions.explanation: HSE inspectors have legal powers of entry without notice, so they can arrive on site unannounced at any reasonable time. Requiring appointments or escorts would let unsafe work be hidden before they arrive, defeating the purpose of enforcement.

questions.prompt: A Prohibition Notice means:

options.B: When you finish the work you must not start again
options.C: Work is to stop for that day only
options.D: Work may continue until the end of the day

questions.explanation: The work activity covered by the prohibition notice must cease, until the identified danger is removed.

questions.prompt: In what circumstances can an HSE Improvement Notice be issued?

options.B: If there is a breach of legal requirements
options.C: Only between Monday and Friday on site

questions.explanation: An Improvement Notice is served when an inspector believes a person is breaching health and safety law, or has breached it in a way likely to continue. It formally requires the breach to be put right within a stated time.

questions.prompt: What is an "Improvement Notice"?

options.A: A notice from the client to the principal contractor to speed up the work
options.B: A notice issued by a Building Control Officer to deepen foundations
options.C: A notice issued by an HSE/local authority Inspector to enforce compliance with health and safety legislation
options.D: A notice issued by the site principal contractor to tidy up the site

questions.explanation: An Improvement Notice is a formal enforcement document from an HSE or local authority inspector requiring a duty holder to remedy a breach of health and safety legislation within a set period. It compels compliance rather than just advising or speeding up work.

questions.prompt: If a Health and Safety Executive Inspector issues a "Prohibition Notice", this means that:

options.A: Specific work activities, highlighted on the notice, must stop
options.B: The HSE must supervise all work from then on
options.C: The HSE must supervise the work covered by the notice
options.D: The Site Manager can choose whether or not to ignore the notice

questions.explanation: Prohibition notices are intended to Stop activities which can cause serious injury.

questions.prompt: Employers are required to provide information to their employees on their health and safety rights and responsibilities and how to get advice by:

options.A: Displaying a poster or giving them leaflets approved by the HSE
options.C: Making them read the company health and safety policy
options.D: Telling them verbally when they start work for them

questions.explanation: This is a requirement of the Health and Safety Information for Employees Regulations (as amended).

questions.prompt: Who is responsible for signing a Company Safety Policy?
questions.explanation: The Health and Safety at Work Act requires the most senior member of management to sign the health and safety policy statement.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following must be in a company's written Health and Safety Policy:

options.A: Aims and objectives of the company
options.C: Name of the Health and Safety Adviser
options.D: Organization and arrangements in force for carrying out the health and safety policy

questions.explanation: This is a specific requirement of the Health and Safety at Work Act.

questions.prompt: Employers have to produce a written Health and Safety Policy statement when:

options.D: They employ five people or more

questions.explanation: This is a specific requirement of the Health and Safety at Work Act.

questions.prompt: Companies employing five or more people must have a written Health and Safety Policy because:

options.B: The Social Security Act requires it
options.C: The principal contractor gives them work on site

questions.explanation: Under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, any employer with five or more employees must have a written safety policy setting out their arrangements and how risks are managed, so responsibilities are clear and recorded rather than left informal.

questions.prompt: What do the letters HSE stand for?
questions.explanation: Health and Safety Executive is correct because electrical safety depends on preventing contact with live parts, using the right supply/protection, and taking damaged equipment out of service. Isolation or reporting beats continuing with an unsafe tool.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety Executive is:

options.A: Part of the National Health Service
options.C: The jury in health and safety court cases
options.D: The regulatory body for the promotion of health and safety at work

questions.explanation: The Health and Safety Executive is part of the Department for Work and Pensions.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety at Work Act requires employers to provide what for their employees?
questions.explanation: This is a specific requirement of Section 2 of the Health and Safety at Work Act.

questions.prompt: What do the letters CDM stand for?

options.D: Control of Demolition and Management Regulations

questions.explanation: The CDM Regulations impose duties to manage construction projects, ensure physical safeguards are provided to prevent danger during such projects and that adequate welfare facilities are provided.

questions.prompt: Identify one method of enforcing regulations that are available to the Health and Safety Executive:
questions.explanation: An Improvement Notice is a genuine HSE enforcement tool requiring a breach of health and safety law to be corrected within a set time. The other options are invented; the HSE enforces through Improvement and Prohibition Notices, not insurance or obstruction notices.

questions.prompt: Why should different types of waste be separated on site?

options.A: So the local council can charge Landfill Tax
options.B: So the main contractor can check what's being thrown away
options.C: So waste can be recovered more easily
options.D: They will take up less room in the skip

questions.explanation: This is good practice, since waste recovery can save both energy and materials, compared to creating brand new materials or items. It will also cut the amount of waste that goes to landfill. If the waste is classed as hazardous (special waste in Scotland) then the effective separation of different wastes is a legal requirement.

questions.prompt: When storing liquids (such as oils, fuels or chemicals) on-site, what must you do?

options.B: Ensure the liquid material is stored safely and securely, and out of the way of site traffic
options.C: Keep the tops off, to prevent pressure from building up
options.D: Use a transparent container so you can check how much liquid is in it

questions.explanation: Any spillage could get into the ground or drains, which is likely to be an offence under environmental legislation.

questions.prompt: What can help to prevent harm to the environment from oil spillages?

options.A: A supply of water to flush the spill away
options.C: Store oils in an area that can catch any spills, such as a bund or a drip tray.
options.D: Turning liquid containers upside down so the top can't come off

questions.explanation: The use of a bund (fully walled storage area) or a drip tray will help any spillage to be contained in a small area for clear up. Any spillage could get into the ground or drains, which is likely to be an offence under environmental legislation.

questions.prompt: You need to clean up some oil that has leaked from machinery onto the ground. What is the right way to do this?

options.A: Put it under some off-cuts so that the oil cannot be seen
options.B: Put the oily contaminated soil into a suitable container that takes hazardous waste
options.C: Put the oily contaminated soil into the general waste skip
options.D: Wash the oil away with water and detergent

questions.explanation: Oil-contaminated wastes are classified as hazardous/special waste in waste legislation. The Hazardous Waste Regulations (Special Waste Regulations in Scotland) require such waste to be properly segregated or otherwise treated, and then recovered or disposed of in an approved way. Following the other options would be an offence under waste legislation.

questions.prompt: Other site workers are complaining that you are generating too much dust. What should you do?

options.A: Ignore them - it's none of their business
options.B: Issue the other site workers with dust masks
options.C: Stop work and inform your supervisor
options.D: Tell them you have nearly finished

questions.explanation: Excessive dust may be a health hazard to you and those around you, but even if it is not a health hazard, excessive dust can be a 'statutory nuisance (under the Environmental Protection Act). Even when it is not a statutory nuisance, it can lead to complaints from neighbours and possible damage to neighbouring property.

questions.prompt: Who needs to understand relevant environmental risks on a construction site?

options.B: Only the environmental clerk of works

questions.explanation: The actions of everyone on site determine how well the risks to the environment (such as water pollution, or creating a local nuisance) are controlled.

questions.prompt: Under environmental law, which statement is true?

options.A: Companies and individuals can be prosecuted if they do not follow the law
options.B: Companies can be prosecuted, but not individuals
options.C: It is legal to disturb protected species' habitats
options.D: It is legal to transport business waste without proper paperwork

questions.explanation: Most environmental law is enforced against companies, but the regulator in the relevant part of the UK (the Environment Agency, SEPA or NIEA) can also prosecute company officers and even have powers to prosecute employees if they wilfully contribute to environmental harm.

questions.prompt: Do individuals have any responsibility for sustainability when on site?

options.A: No, it is a matter for the Environment Agency/NIEA/SEPA
options.B: No, it is dealt with by the site manager
options.C: Only on sites where there is asbestos

questions.explanation: Your responsibility is to follow the site and company rules aimed at environmental protection and sustainability, and to help your company to comply with relevant legal requirements, such as the need to segregate waste properly (e.g. so that it can be recovered).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT best practice from a sustainability point of view?

options.A: Looking after the people working on or near the site
options.C: Saving materials, fuel, water and energy
options.D: Sending unused and waste copper cables to landfill

questions.explanation: Option D) would be wasting a valuable natural resource (copper) that could be effectively recovered for later use or recycling. Reusing or recycling copper has less environmental impact than mining and extracting new copper reserves.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does NOT help sustainability during construction projects?

options.B: Leaving engines and motors running when they are not needed
options.D: Vehicle sharing or using public transport to get to work

questions.explanation: Leaving engines and motors running wastes fuel, creates avoidable emissions and adds unnecessary site noise. Switching plant off when it is not needed is the sustainable choice.

questions.prompt: Which of the following should you do on site in the interest of sustainability?

options.B: Comply with site instructions on handling waste materials
options.C: Pour waste liquids down a drain off-site
options.D: Run plant and equipment when they are not needed

questions.explanation: Your actions will help your company, and others working on site, to achieve more sustainable work practices, such as waste recovery.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT part of 'environmentally-friendly' construction?

options.A: Creating a dust nuisance to residents in neighbouring properties
options.B: Minimising the amount of waste you create during a job

questions.explanation: Neighbours outside the site are an important part of the wider environment. They may be affected by nuisance (such as noise, dust or even light at night), and they may complain to the client, main contractor or the local enforcing authority. Creating certain types of nuisance is an offence under the Environmental Protection Act.

questions.prompt: From an environmental point of view, why should materials be reused, where possible?

options.A: A lot of energy and raw materials go into making most construction products
options.B: It makes less mess on site

questions.explanation: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the re-use of materials can also contribute to effective waste management.

questions.prompt: Which action will help to minimise waste?

options.A: Always order much more than usually required - just in case you need it
options.B: Leave materials unprotected in the rain
options.C: Only take or open what you need and return or reseal anything left over
options.D: Use new materials/packs at the beginning of each day

questions.explanation: The hierarchy for managing waste is to reduce/reuse/recover. Reducing the amount of waste is therefore the first priority.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is good environmental practice?

options.A: Leaving motors running when they are not needed
options.B: Leaving skips uncovered in wet weather

questions.explanation: This is good practice, since it will help with waste recovery. If the waste is classified as hazardous waste (special waste in Scotland) proper segregation is also a legal requirement.

questions.prompt: Do individuals have any responsibility for minimising the amount of waste created on site?

options.A: No, it's the responsibility of the client
options.B: Only during site clean-up, at the end of the project
options.C: Only if asbestos removal is being carried out
options.D: Yes, everyone on site has this responsibility

questions.explanation: Your actions will help your company, and others on site, to procure sensibly and to organise the job so that materials and substances are not wasted. Waste reduction is the best option when trying to manage site waste.

questions.prompt: If you have unused material left, what should you do before you consider putting non-hazardous waste items into a skip?

options.A: Check whether someone else on your team can make use of it
options.B: Make sure there is a label on it
options.C: Put it in a plastic bag and put it in a skip

questions.explanation: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the reuse of waste materials is much better than disposal, which is the most expensive option and which should be the last resort. Reuse is a better waste management option than recovery.

questions.prompt: You are on site and you need to dispose of some waste liquid that has oil in it and you are not sure what to do with it. What should you do?

options.A: Ask your supervisor about the correct way to deal with this waste.
options.B: Dispose of it in a sealed container into the site skip
options.C: Pour it onto the ground, it will soak away
options.D: Take it outside and set light to it

questions.explanation: Dealing with hazardous/special waste will include proper storage and segregation before it is taken away by an authorized waste carrier as required by environmental legislation. An oil spillage could also get into the ground or drains, which may also be an offence under environmental law. Burning waste on site is also an offence, under air pollution legislation, and can lead to local complaints.

questions.prompt: How should you get rid of hazardous/special waste?

options.A: In accordance with the correct site waste rules
